Can an ugly anime character still be popular?

Absolutely, and some of the most popular characters around are proof. Memorable beats pretty every time. A distinctive ugly design gives a character instant recognition, and when it is paired with a great personality, fans latch on even harder than they would for one more interchangeable handsome face.

Title: Ranking the 20 Best Anime Characters of All Time
Summary: Count down 20 best anime characters ranked on writing, growth, and staying power, with Guts and Lelouch up top. 🏆
Meta Title: The 20 Best Anime Characters of All Time, Ranked
Meta Description: Settle the best anime characters debate with 20 picks ranked on writing and depth, not power levels. Come hang out with Kaminari for more.
Author: devin-morris
Content:
Ask a room full of fans to name the best anime characters and you will not get a list. You will get into an argument, and it will run until someone's voice gives out. Half the fun is the argument itself. Greatness in anime was never about who hits hardest, and the endless strongest-character power-scaling wars miss the point completely. The best anime characters are the ones who would still matter with their powers switched off: the writing, the growth, the moments that quietly rearranged how you think about a story.

So this is a ranking built on that idea. Not raw strength and not raw fame, but writing, growth, and the kind of presence that outlives the show. The question of who is the greatest anime character of all time never really settles, and honestly it should not, but some names belong in any serious version of the conversation, and we are going to make the case for each of them.

What follows is a full countdown, ranked one through twenty on writing, depth, and staying power, and built less as a list of popular anime characters sorted by vote count than as a case for why each of these twenty endures. Reasonable fans will reorder the middle. The names themselves are hard to argue with.

The 20 best anime characters, ranked

Every ranking like this is a snapshot of an argument in motion, so treat the order as a strong opening bid, not gospel. Every argument about the best anime characters ever eventually circles back to these names, ranked on the strength of their writing, the depth of their arc, and how much they still matter as characters (not how famous they got). The top 10 anime characters of all time sit up front, and the rest of the top anime characters of all time follow right behind, each earning the spot on the same terms.

1. Guts

Anime: Berserk

Guts begins as a mercenary with nothing and becomes the definitive portrait of a person who refuses to let suffering have the final word. Nobody in anime has been put through more, and nobody keeps getting back up quite like him. Strip away the giant sword and the dark fantasy and he is still the most complete character study the medium has produced, which is exactly why he takes the top spot.

2. Lelouch vi Britannia

Anime: Code Geass

An exiled prince wages a one-man revolution so layered that his final act still starts fights over whether he is a hero or the grandest villain of his own story. Every scheme, every mask, every sacrifice is plotted with a precision most shows never even attempt. Lelouch is what happens when a writer trusts the audience to keep up.

3. Light Yagami

Anime: Death Note

A straight-A student finds a notebook that kills and slowly talks himself into playing god. Light's rot from idealist to monster is some of the tightest writing anime has ever produced, without a wasted scene in the descent. You watch a brilliant boy argue himself into damnation and follow every step of the logic.

4. Vegeta

Anime: Dragon Ball

The road from genocidal prince to devoted family man is the finest redemption arc shonen has ever attempted, earned across decades instead of handed over cheap. Vegeta never stops being proud and never stops being difficult, and that stubbornness is exactly what makes the growth land. He changes without ever betraying who he is.

5. Edward Elric

Anime: Fullmetal Alchemist

A boy pays for his arrogance in actual flesh and then spends the whole series earning his way back toward something like peace. Every beat of Ed's story is built on a rule the writing refuses to break, and the result is the most thematically airtight arc on this list. Equivalent exchange, all the way down.

6. Eren Yeager

Anime: Attack on Titan

A boy wants freedom so badly that he walks straight into becoming the thing he hated. Eren's arc is bleak, divisive, and unforgettable, the rare shonen lead whose ending fans will keep arguing about for as long as the medium exists. Love it or loathe it, nobody else attempted anything this bold.

7. Monkey D. Luffy

Anime: One Piece

Across more than a thousand episodes, Luffy has never once gone stale, because his freedom-above-everything code makes every choice land the same way (pure) and the writing never betrays it. He is proof that consistency, done right, is its own kind of greatness. Nobody has carried a story this long without wobbling.

8. Itachi Uchiha

Anime: Naruto

Itachi turns one revealed truth into anime's most gutting reversal, a character the whole fandom mourned the instant they understood what he had actually done. Recontextualizing an entire person with a single flashback is a trick most writers never pull off. He is still the gold standard for the tragic double life.

9. Levi Ackerman

Anime: Attack on Titan

Humanity's strongest soldier is a man of few words and enormous loss whose restraint does more character work in a single glance than most leads manage across a whole season. Levi never leads his series and still walks off as everyone's favorite, and it is the writing, not the sword work, that earns it.

10. Goku

Anime: Dragon Ball

Goku is the foundation the rest of shonen was built on, and leaving him off a list like this would be dishonest. His greatness runs more on heart than depth, and that is not a knock: he is not the most complex character here, and he was never trying to be. He is the purest version of the never-stop-climbing spirit that shaped everything that came after.

11. Griffith

Anime: Berserk

A charismatic dreamer makes a single choice that becomes one of the most devastating betrayals in all of fiction. Griffith is hard to even discuss without flinching, which is the real measure of how well he is written. Few characters ever make you understand a monster this completely.

12. Frieren

Anime: Frieren: Beyond Journey's End

An elf mage outlives everyone she loves and spends her story learning, far too late, what those people actually meant to her. Frieren flips the whole hero's-journey formula on its head, and her quiet grief is some of the most mature storytelling anime has ever tried. Proof the medium is still writing genuinely new kinds of characters.

13. Naruto Uzumaki

Anime: Naruto

Naruto turns being the outcast into the most resonant underdog story in anime, a kid screaming into the void until his whole village finally hears him. The loneliness sitting under all that noise is what makes him land. Take away the ninja powers and the ache is still real.

14. Shinji Ikari

Anime: Neon Genesis Evangelion

The most psychologically raw protagonist anime has ever centered a series on, a frightened kid whose refusal to be a hero became one of the medium's most honest studies of depression and self-worth. Loving him is not easy, and understanding him is the entire point.

15. Satoru Gojo

Anime: Jujutsu Kaisen

The rare character whose swagger is the mask rather than the man, the strongest sorcerer alive written with a buried loneliness and a fate that recontextualizes every cocky grin he throws. Gojo is the modern great who proves charisma and real depth were never opposites.

16. Killua Zoldyck

Anime: Hunter x Hunter

That rare best-friend character written with far more nuance than most leads ever get, an ex-assassin kid slowly learning how to choose his own heart. Killua's quiet fight against everything he was raised to be is one of the most tender arcs anime has to offer.

17. Sosuke Aizen

Anime: Bleach

A mastermind so composed he makes ten seasons feel like they went precisely according to his plan. Aizen earns his spot on pure audacity, the villain who was always five steps ahead and somehow made you believe it. Presence is a writing skill, and almost nobody has more of it.

18. Kakashi Hatake

Anime: Naruto

The mentor everyone wishes they had, the mask-and-one-eye enigma whose easy calm hides far more grief than he ever lets show. Kakashi carries an entire tragic backstory in his body language, and the restraint is exactly what makes him unforgettable.

19. Denji

Anime: Chainsaw Man

The anti-Goku: a broke, hormonal, deeply human teenager who just wants a normal life and keeps getting handed a chainsaw instead. Denji is more relatable than any polished hero could hope to be, and that lowness is the point. Greatness does not have to look noble.

20. Power

Anime: Chainsaw Man

The blood-fiend chaos gremlin who rounds out the new class, proof that a character can be selfish, loud, and completely ridiculous and still wreck you when it counts. Power is the rare comic-relief character whose best moment leaves the whole room silent.

Greatness outlasts the power level

Run back through the whole list and the strongest characters are almost never the ones people cry over. That is the quiet truth sitting under every version of this debate. The best anime characters of all time endure because of what they mean, not what they can lift, and the argument over the best anime characters ever will keep raging precisely because greatness refuses to fit inside a tier list. Guts, Lelouch, Luffy, Vegeta, and the rest earned their place by making us feel something no power level, and no popularity ranking, could ever measure. Pick your own number one. Just be ready to defend it, because everyone else already picked theirs.

If breaking down what actually makes a character great sounds like a good time to you, you will feel right at home at Kaminari. Our newsletter drops the week's anime news, reviews, and character deep-dives straight into your inbox, free, over at Kaminari. Come argue about the rankings with a few thousand fans who care about this stuff as much as you do.

Frequently asked questions

Who is the best anime character?

It depends on what you weigh most, but if best means the strongest writing and the deepest arc, which is how we ranked it, Guts, Lelouch, and Light Yagami lead the pack. Goku is the most influential and probably the most famous character anime has ever produced, though fame and influence are their own axis, separate from who is actually written best. The honest answer is that the best anime character is the one whose story hit you hardest, and the debate is half the reason we love this medium.

What makes an anime character the best?

Not raw power. The characters who last are the ones with strong writing, real growth, and a presence that shapes the story around them. A great design and a memorable voice help, but the deciding factor is whether you still think about them long after the credits roll. Strength fades from memory; a well-written arc does not.

Are the best anime characters the same as the strongest?

Almost never, and treating the two as one thing is the most common mistake in these rankings. The strongest anime characters are a power-scaling conversation about who wins a fight, while the best anime characters are about craft and meaning. Plenty of the greatest characters ever written would lose a straight brawl to some reality-warping newcomer, and still be remembered long after that newcomer is forgotten.

Who are the best modern anime characters?

The current class is stacked. Satoru Gojo, Frieren, Denji, and Power lead the way, alongside names like Makima and Yuji Itadori. They are proof that the medium is still minting all-time greats rather than coasting on the classics.

What are the top 5 anime characters of all time?

By our ranking, the top 5 anime characters of all time are Guts, Lelouch vi Britannia, Light Yagami, Vegeta, and Edward Elric. Reasonable fans will swap a couple of those out, and that is exactly how it should be.

Title: 20 Beginner-Friendly Anime Characters To Draw, Perfect for Leveling Up Your Art
Summary: Line up 20 anime characters to draw sorted by difficulty, easy mascots up through cooler boss-level picks, plus starter tips. ✏️
Meta Title: Anime Characters to Draw: 20 Easy Picks by Level
Meta Description: Find the anime characters to draw at any skill level, sorted from easy mascots to cooler picks. Check out Kaminari for more anime guides.
Author: devin-morris
Content:
The best anime characters to draw are the ones you can actually finish. Simple shapes, a silhouette you recognize on sight, one or two signature details that carry the whole design. Get those right and you walk away with a sketch worth keeping instead of a page you want to hide. That is the real filter for a beginner-friendly pick, and it has nothing to do with how strong or popular the character happens to be.

We rounded up twenty of our favorite anime characters to draw and sorted them by difficulty, from mascots you can knock out in five minutes to cooler picks worth leveling up for. Every one comes with the reason it works on paper and a quick tip on where to lay your first line, so you are not just staring at a finished drawing wondering how anyone got there.

If you need anime characters drawing ideas, a quick warm-up, or a proper challenge, there is something below at your level. We also tucked a short how-to section near the end for the fundamentals that sharpen every anime sketch. Grab a pencil and let's get into it.

Easy anime characters to draw

These are the picks to start with. Bold shapes, minimal detail, and faces that forgive a shaky line. If you can draw a circle and a couple of triangles, you can handle everyone in this group.

1. Totoro

Anime: My Neighbor Totoro

Totoro is basically a giant fuzzy bean, and that is the whole secret. Start with one big rounded oval for the body, add two triangle ears up top, then drop in the tiny eyes and that wide whiskery grin. The proportions are so soft that nothing has to be precise, which makes him the perfect first sketch of any session.

2. Pikachu

Anime: Pokémon

Nothing says warm-up like Pikachu. A rounded body, two long pointed ears with black tips, the zigzag tail, and those red cheek circles do all the work. Begin with an egg shape for the body and build outward. If your tail already looks like a lightning bolt, you are basically there.

3. Anya Forger

Anime: Spy x Family

Anya is a masterclass in getting expression out of almost nothing. Her head is a simple round shape, her eyes are big and glassy, and the two little hair points and rounded buns are the details that make her unmistakable. Nail the wide-eyed look and her whole scheming-toddler charm comes through without any fancy construction.

4. Saitama

Anime: One Punch Man

Saitama might be the most beginner-proof face in all of anime. An egg-shaped head, two dot eyes, a straight line for a mouth, and you are done. The trick is trusting the simplicity, because the harder you resist adding detail, the more he actually looks like himself.

5. Pochita

Anime: Chainsaw Man

Pochita is pure geometry with a heartbeat. The little orange chainsaw-pup is built from circles and a chunky snout, with a pull-cord poking out of his head and a round eye on each side. He is soft enough to warm up with and iconic enough that people clock him instantly.

6. Shinnosuke Nohara

Anime: Crayon Shin-chan

Shin-chan looks like a kid drew him, which is exactly why he is a joy for beginners. Blocky head, thick caterpillar eyebrows, tiny dot eyes, a cheeky grin. Keep the lines loose and a little wonky, because a too-clean Shin-chan somehow ends up looking wrong.

7. Tony Tony Chopper

Anime: One Piece

Chopper is what happens when a reindeer gets designed to be maximally huggable. The oversized pink hat, round face, and little antlers all stack up from a handful of soft shapes. Start with the hat as its own big blob, since it frames everything else and does most of the identifying for you.

Fun anime characters to draw

Ready to add a bit more? These fun anime characters to draw ask for some hair detail or a signature prop, and the payoff is a character that really reads on the page. Good territory once the basics feel comfortable.

8. Monkey D. Luffy

Anime: One Piece

Luffy is the friendliest step up on this list. His face is simple and round, the scar under his eye is two quick strokes, and the straw hat does most of the identifying before you even finish the smile. Block the hat and head together first, then let that huge grin set the whole mood.

9. Nezuko Kamado

Anime: Demon Slayer

Nezuko is a favorite because her signature details carry the drawing. The bamboo muzzle strap, the long flowing hair with its lighter tips, and the checkered kimono collar tell you exactly who she is. Get the hair silhouette and the bamboo in place first, and everything else falls into line.

10. Zenitsu Agatsuma

Anime: Demon Slayer

Zenitsu is a blast because his panic is half the drawing. Swept-forward yellow hair, worried eyebrows, and the triangle-patterned haori give you a character bursting with personality. Start calm with the head shape, then push the expression as far as you dare.

11. Naruto Uzumaki

Anime: Naruto

Naruto is the gateway shonen sketch. Spiky hair in clear chunks, the forehead protector as a simple band, three whisker marks per cheek. Draw the hair as a handful of solid shapes rather than individual strands and the whole thing clicks together fast.

12. Killua Zoldyck

Anime: Hunter x Hunter

Killua keeps things clean. Messy white hair drawn as loose spikes, a relaxed face, and almost no clutter to trip over. He is proof that a cool character does not need heavy detail, just a confident silhouette and a slightly mischievous look.

13. Roronoa Zoro

Anime: One Piece

Zoro bridges fun and cool. Short green hair, three little earrings on one side, a scar over the left eye, and a bandana when he means business. Each of those is a small, satisfying detail, and together they make him instantly readable without much anatomy at all.

14. Frieren

Anime: Frieren: Beyond Journey's End

Frieren has one of the calmest, most elegant designs on this list. Long pale hair tied up with a few loose strands, pointed elf ears, a soft steady expression, and a simple mage's outfit. The stillness is both the challenge and the reward: less motion, more care in every line.

Cool anime characters to draw

Reach for this tier when you want cool anime stuff to draw that still stays achievable. A little more attitude, a little more detail, but every pick is built on the same shape-first logic as the easy ones.

15. Satoru Gojo

Anime: Jujutsu Kaisen

Here is a secret: Gojo is easier than he looks, because the blindfold lets you skip the hardest part of any anime face. Spiky white hair, the wrapped blindfold, a smug half-smile, and you have got the strongest sorcerer alive. Nail the hair volume and the cloth folds and he lands every time.

16. Levi Ackerman

Anime: Attack on Titan

Levi is all sharp angles and clean lines. The undercut hair, the loose cravat, and those flat serious eyes give him a cool that reads even in a rough sketch. Keep everything crisp and controlled, because a sloppy Levi loses the entire vibe.

17. Hisoka

Anime: Hunter x Hunter

Hisoka is a personality you draw more than a body. Slicked-back hair, a star and a teardrop painted on his face, and a playing-card motif you can scatter around him. Those two face marks are the fastest way to make a sketch unmistakably him, so lay them in early.

18. Guts

Anime: Berserk

Guts is the boss level of this list, and the giant sword does half the work. That massive slab of a blade is an iconic silhouette on its own, so build the drawing around it first, then add the scarred face, the prosthetic arm, and the heavy armor. Ambitious, but hugely satisfying when it all comes together.

19. Ichigo Kurosaki

Anime: Bleach

Ichigo gives you a cool payoff for moderate effort. Bright spiky orange hair, a permanent scowl, the flowing black shinigami robes, and the oversized cleaver slung behind him. Start with the hair and the sword as your two anchors and let the rest hang off them.

20. Denji

Anime: Chainsaw Man

Denji is a perfect closer because you get two drawings in one. Base Denji is a scruffy, simple-faced teen, easy enough for anyone. His Chainsaw Man form, with the blades bursting from his head and arms, is one of the coolest things on this whole list to pull off. Work up to the transformation and you will feel every bit of that progress.

How to draw awesome anime characters (quick tips)

Picking the character is half the battle. The rest comes down to a few habits that make every sketch stronger. If you want to know how to draw great anime characters faster, this is where it starts.

Build from basic shapes before you commit to a single clean line. A circle for the skull, a soft line for the jaw, and simple blocks for the body give you a frame that keeps proportions honest. Treat the hair as one big silhouette first, then carve the chunks out of it, instead of drawing strand by strand and hoping it adds up. Let the eyes carry the expression, since in anime they do most of the emotional work, and keep your first pass light so you can fix mistakes without a fight. Loose, confident, and shape-first beats slow and stiff every single time.

Honorable mentions

A few more worth keeping on your practice page: Megumi Fushiguro for that spiky, sculptural hair, Tanjiro Kamado for checkered-pattern practice, Jigglypuff for a pure round-shape warm-up, and chibi versions of literally anyone when you want the fun without the anatomy. None quite cracked the top twenty, but each one earns its spot in a sketchbook.

Fill the page and keep going

The fastest way to get better is to pick one character above and actually draw it, then draw it again tomorrow. Start in the easy tier, steal the starting tips, and let the cool picks pull you forward as your confidence grows. Every artist you admire began with wobbly ovals and one favorite character they could not stop sketching.

If you want more anime in your week between drawing sessions, come hang out with us at Kaminari, where our newsletter rounds up the news, reviews, and character breakdowns worth your time. Bring your sketchbook. We will bring the hype.

FAQs

What anime characters to draw when you are starting out?

Start with the simplest shapes. Totoro, Pikachu, Anya Forger, Saitama, and Pochita are all built from circles and a couple of signature details. They read instantly and forgive a shaky line, which is exactly what you want early on.

What anime is easy to draw for beginners?

Anything with bold, simple shapes and minimal fine detail. Mascot-style designs like Totoro and Pikachu, and minimalist faces like Saitama, are the easiest anime to draw because a few strokes already look right. Chibi versions of any character work too.

How do you start drawing an anime character?

Block in basic shapes first: a circle for the head, a line for the jaw, and simple forms for the body. Treat the hair as one silhouette before adding chunks, and let the eyes anchor the expression. Keep the first pass light so mistakes are easy to fix.

Who is the easiest anime character to draw?

Saitama from One Punch Man is the usual answer. An egg-shaped head, two dots, and a line for a mouth is a complete, recognizable character. Totoro and Pikachu sit right behind him for the same reason: unmistakable shapes, almost no detail.

Looking for cool anime stuff to draw?

Once the basics click, reach for characters with strong silhouettes and signature props: Gojo's blindfold, Levi's cravat, Guts and his giant sword, or Ichigo with his oversized blade. Big iconic shapes look impressive on the page even before you add any polish.

Title: 20 Strongest Anime Characters Ranked by Sheer Muscle and Willpower
Summary: Rank 20 strongest anime characters on raw muscle and willpower, no power-scaling gods, with Guts up top. 💪
Meta Title: Strongest Anime Characters: Top 20, Ranked
Meta Description: See the strongest anime characters ranked on muscle and willpower, not reality-warping hax. Head to Kaminari for more anime lists.
Author: devin-morris
Content:
Ask the internet for the strongest anime characters and you drown in the same answer: gods who erase universes, slimes who rewrite reality, characters so “powerful” the fight ends before it starts. We find that boring. The strongest anime character ever, to us, is the one you can feel in your bones, raw physical power and a will that refuses to break, not whoever owns the most broken ability.

So this strongest anime characters list skips the power-scaling gods and ranks on two things that actually mean strong: physical might and force of will. The big strong anime characters who win with muscle, and the ones whose spirit simply outlasts everything thrown at them. Anyone who brings both, like our number one, sits at the very top.

Our top 10 strongest anime characters lead the way, with ten more right behind. Every pick earns its rank on strength you can see or heart you can feel, never on a hax ability that skips the fight. Let's get into it.

The 20 strongest anime characters, ranked

We ranked these on raw physical strength and sheer willpower, weighted so anyone who brings both climbs highest. No universe-erasers, no reality-warpers, just power you could feel if you were standing in the room.

1. Guts

Anime: Berserk

Guts is the answer to this entire question. He swings a slab of iron the size of a grown man like it weighs nothing, takes wounds that would kill anyone else, and gets up every single time because stopping never occurs to him. Physical monster, unbreakable will, zero magic tricks. If strength means muscle and refusal in equal measure, nobody on earth touches him.

2. All Might

Anime: My Hero Academia

All Might is what raw physical power looks like when it decides to be a hero. His punches move the weather. United States of Smash does not bend reality, it just hits harder than anything has a right to. Even hollowed out and running on fumes, the Symbol of Peace threw one last fist that an entire nation felt.

3. Yujiro Hanma

Anime: Baki Hanma

They call Yujiro the strongest creature on Earth, and his series means it literally. Here is a man who wrestles the planet itself, fights off a country's military for fun, and stops an earthquake with a stance. No powers, no abilities, just a human body pushed to a place that should not be possible.

4. Escanor

Anime: The Seven Deadly Sins

At high noon, Escanor is untouchable. His strength climbs with the sun until “The One” stands as the single most physically overwhelming hour in anime. It is his pride that fuels it, a will so absolute it swells his own body into a giant. Catch him at midnight and he is meek. Catch him at noon and run.

5. Asta

Anime: Black Clover

Asta is the purest pick on this list, because he was born with zero magic in a world that runs on it. What he has instead is a body forged by swinging heavy swords for years and a will that flat refuses to quit. He out-works, out-lasts, and out-shouts everyone in the room. Strength without a single shortcut.

6. Edward Newgate

Anime: One Piece

Whitebeard held the title of strongest man in the world, and he looked every inch of it. A mountain of a man who fought a war half-dead and still stood, still terrified an entire navy. His presence alone bent the battlefield. Even at the very end, he never took a single step backward.

7. Tsunade

Anime: Naruto

Tsunade hits harder than almost anyone in her world, full stop. One focused punch cracks open the ground and sends monsters flying, which is why she is the benchmark for raw physical power among the legendary Sannin. Behind the muscle is a woman who carried unbearable loss and still stood back up to lead a whole village. Grit and force in equal measure.

8. Kenshiro

Anime: Fist of the North Star

Kenshiro is physical mastery sharpened into an art. His fists find the pressure points that end a fight in seconds, and his frame carries scars most people would not survive collecting. Calm, immovable, and lethal, he is the blueprint every stoic powerhouse after him quietly borrowed from.

9. Might Guy

Anime: Naruto

Might Guy cannot use a lick of ninjutsu, and he still pushed a god to the edge of death. Opening all Eight Gates and unleashing Night Guy is the most heroic act of pure physical effort in the series, a technique that burns his own life for one unstoppable kick. That is strength measured in sacrifice.

10. Mikasa Ackerman

Anime: Attack on Titan

Mikasa is the strongest soldier of her generation, and it is not close. Ackerman blood gives her a physical edge, but it is her refusal to lose the people she loves that turns her into a one-woman army. Precise, relentless, and steady when everyone around her is falling apart.

11. Maki Zenin

Anime: Jujutsu Kaisen

Maki is the female answer to the powerless powerhouse. Born into a sorcerer clan with almost no cursed energy, she was written off her whole life, so she forged her body and her weapon skill into something that leaves full-blown sorcerers eating dust. Her strength is pure physical work sharpened by a will to prove every doubter wrong. She earns this spot the hard way.

12. Alex Louis Armstrong

Anime: Fullmetal Alchemist

The Strong Arm Alchemist wears his strength on his sleeve, mostly because his sleeves keep exploding off. Armstrong's alchemy is really just a delivery system for raw muscle, generations of it, passed proudly down the family line. He is the rare powerhouse who is as warm as he is physically enormous.

13. Ippo Makunouchi

Anime: Hajime no Ippo

Ippo is the most grounded name here, and that is exactly why he belongs. No powers, no fantasy, just a shy kid who turned his fists into wrecking balls through pure repetition. His body soaks up punishment and answers with a Dempsey Roll that ends nights early. Real strength, no asterisks.

14. Yoruichi Shihouin

Anime: Bleach

Yoruichi fights with her hands and her speed, and she rarely needs anything else. The Flash Goddess is a hand-to-hand master quick enough to seem like she is in three places at once and strong enough to end most fights before they start. Calm, playful, and fully in control, she is proof that raw physical combat still beats a flashy special move.

15. Yuji Itadori

Anime: Jujutsu Kaisen

Yuji hits like a truck and refuses to fold, which is the whole point of him. His physical strength was freakish before any curse got involved, and his real weapon is a heart that keeps choosing to save people no matter the cost to himself. Muscle and mercy in the same body.

16. Erza Scarlet

Anime: Fairy Tail

Erza is willpower wearing armor. Titania has taken beatings that would end most fighters and kept marching forward on grit alone, guarding her guild like her life depends on it. Her strength is equal parts physical force and a spine that simply will not bend. Few characters carry a room the way she does.

17. Simon

Anime: Tengen Toppa Gurren Lagann

Simon fights with his spirit made solid. Spiral power runs on sheer determination, and nobody digs deeper than the kid who started underground and drilled his way to the stars. His strength grows in exact step with his willpower, the most literal version of this whole list's idea.

18. Gon Freecss

Anime: Hunter x Hunter

Gon's strength is terrifying because of what it costs. Faced with losing someone he loved, he bet his entire future on a single burst of overwhelming power, aging himself into a monster out of pure will. It is the darkest example of heart as a weapon, and one of the hardest to forget.

19. Tanjiro Kamado

Anime: Demon Slayer

Tanjiro carries impossible weight and never lets it break his kindness, which is its own kind of strength. His body endures beatings that should end him, and his resolve to protect his sister drags him through every wall in his path. Gentle on the outside, iron all the way underneath.

20. Eren Yeager

Anime: Attack on Titan

Eren's strength is his will bent past the breaking point. The same drive that made him a hero eventually made him something far more frightening, a boy who would move the earth itself before he would stop. Terrifying, tragic, and impossible to look away from.

Honorable mentions

A few more tough anime characters who just missed the cut: Rock Lee and his bottomless taijutsu grind, Jotaro Kujo leading with his fists, Toriko punching beasts flat, and Sakura Haruno matching her master Tsunade blow for blow. Any one of them could headline a lesser list.

Real strength, no shortcuts

Strip away the reality-warping and the power-scaling charts, and the strongest anime character in all of anime turns out simpler than the internet wants it to be: the one who hits the hardest and refuses to fall. Guts, All Might, Escanor, Asta, every name here won a spot with something you could actually feel, muscle or will or both. That is the kind of strength that sticks with you long after the flashy stuff fades.

If you would rather talk characters than crunch power levels, come trade takes with us at Kaminari, where our newsletter covers the news, reviews, and fights worth caring about. Pull up a seat. The debate is always open.

FAQs

Who's the strongest anime character of all time?

By our measure, which is physical strength and force of will rather than power-scaling, it is Guts from Berserk. He carries a sword bigger than most people, survives the impossible on repeat, and never once considers staying down. Raw power and an unbreakable will in one body is about as strong as it gets.

Is the strongest anime character the same as the strongest being in anime?

Not on this list. The strongest being in anime, by pure power-scaling, is usually some reality-warping god who erases universes without moving. We think that misses what strength actually means. Our picks win with physical might and willpower you can feel, not abilities that end the fight before it begins.

Who are the strongest anime characters by physical strength alone?

For raw muscle, the top of the pile is All Might, Yujiro Hanma, Escanor at high noon, Whitebeard, and Tsunade. These are the bruisers who win with power you could measure in a single punch, no special abilities required.

Who has the strongest willpower in anime?

For sheer will, Asta, Guts, Erza Scarlet, Gon Freecss, and Eren Yeager lead the way. Each one won less through power than through a flat refusal to stop, whether that meant training without magic, guarding a guild to the last, or moving the earth itself.

What's the strongest anime character ever, if you skip the power-scaling gods?

Take away the universe-erasers and the title comes down to a fight between the pure powerhouses and the iron-willed. Our vote goes to Guts, with All Might and Escanor a step behind, because strength built from muscle and heart ages far better than a broken ability ever will.

Title: Ranking the 20 Coolest Blue-Haired Anime Characters
Summary: Round up 20 blue haired anime characters across every shade, heroes, villains, goddesses, and lovable disasters. 💙
Meta Title: The 20 Best Blue Haired Anime Characters
Meta Description: Discover the blue haired anime characters who wear the color best, from loyal Rem to feral Grimmjow. Swing by Kaminari for more anime picks.
Author: devin-morris
Content:
Blue haired anime characters have a way of standing out, and not by accident. In a medium where hair color doubles as personality shorthand, blue tends to land on the calm ones, the cool ones, the fiercely loyal ones, and the occasional lovable disaster. We pulled together twenty of the best, spanning every shade and every kind of character.

Blue comes in every version here. We have got light blue hair anime characters like Aqua and Kuroko, dark blue hair anime characters like Hinata and Rin, more than one anime character with long blue hair, and even a blue spiky hair anime character in Grimmjow. Heroes, villains, goddesses, and disasters, male and female alike.

Some are the most famous blue hair anime characters in the medium, the ones you picture the second the topic comes up. Others are quiet favorites worth discovering. Every pick earns its spot on personality, presence, and the moments that made it matter, not just the color of its hair. Let's get into it.

The 19 best blue haired anime characters

These are our favorites from every corner of anime, the characters who made blue hair unforgettable through who they are, not just how they look. No strict ranking, just twenty who wear the color best.

1. Rem

Anime: Re:Zero

Rem is the character who turned blue hair into a full-blown fandom moment. The devoted maid of the Roswaal mansion went from background player to the center of the “best girl” debate on the strength of one unforgettable confession scene. Fiercely loyal, quietly heartbroken, and impossible not to root for. The short blue bob is iconic, but it is her devotion people remember.

2. Rimuru Tempest

Anime: That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime

Rimuru starts as a slime and ends up running a nation, which is a career glow-up nobody saw coming. In humanoid form, the sky-blue hair and gold eyes are instantly recognizable, but the real draw is a leader who is equal parts kind, ruthless, and weirdly relatable. Few isekai protagonists carry a series this effortlessly.

3. Hinata Hyuga

Anime: Naruto

Hinata spent most of Naruto as the shy girl watching from the sidelines, then quietly became one of its most beloved characters through sheer heart. Her dark indigo hair frames a Hyuga heiress who found her courage the hard way, standing her ground when it counted most. Gentle, brave, and steadier than anyone gives her credit for.

4. Juvia Lockser

Anime: Fairy Tail

Juvia is devotion turned all the way up. Her deep blue hair suits a rain-summoning water mage whose entire personality reorganized itself the moment she met Gray Fullbuster. Obsessive, dramatic, and genuinely powerful once a fight breaks out, she is one of Fairy Tail's most entertaining guild members. Nobody on this list loves harder, for better or worse.

5. Grimmjow Jaegerjaquez

Anime: Bleach

Grimmjow is the blue spiky hair anime character every Bleach fan has a soft spot for. As an Espada, he is pure feral pride, a villain who fights because losing to anyone is unthinkable to him. The electric blue hair matches the energy exactly: unpredictable, aggressive, and always hunting the next challenge.

6. Franky

Anime: One Piece

Franky is the cyborg shipwright who runs on cola and pure enthusiasm, blue hair shaped into whatever ridiculous style the moment calls for. Loud, sentimental, and endlessly loyal to the Straw Hats, he builds the crew everything from warships to weapons, striking a pose the entire time. All heart and horsepower, with a real genius hiding under the muscle.

7. Rei Ayanami

Anime: Neon Genesis Evangelion

Rei is quiet in a way that gets under your skin. The pale blue hair and blank stare made her an instant icon, but the mystery of who she actually is powers some of Evangelion's most haunting moments. Withdrawn, enigmatic, and far more central to the whole story than she first appears.

8. Esdeath

Anime: Akame ga Kill

Esdeath is proof that a villain can walk off with the entire show. A general with light blue hair and a chilling worldview (the strong live, the weak die), she is terrifying and magnetic at the same time. The scariest part is how much fun she clearly seems to be having.

9. Aqua

Anime: KonoSuba

Aqua is a literal goddess who is also a complete disaster, and that is precisely why fans adore her. Flowing light blue hair, a water-molecule hair clip, and absolutely no impulse control. She is supposed to be the party's divine support and spends most of KonoSuba crying, scheming, or making everything worse. Comedy gold.

10. Kuroko Tetsuya

Anime: Kuroko's Basketball

Kuroko is the phantom sixth man, the player nobody notices until the ball is already gone. His pale light blue hair suits a personality so low-key he practically vanishes on the court, which is the whole point of his game. Calm, sharp, and quietly lethal through misdirection.

11. Nagisa Shiota

Anime: Assassination Classroom

Nagisa looks like the gentlest kid in class, right up until he reveals a talent for assassination that unsettles everyone around him. The light blue hair and soft smile hide a genuinely frightening focus. He is the quiet one you absolutely do not want to underestimate.

12. Jellal Fernandes

Anime: Fairy Tail

Jellal is Fairy Tail's tortured antihero, his blue hair marked by that unmistakable red tattoo across one eye. His arc runs from brainwashed villain to a man desperate to atone, and the guilt he carries gives every scene real weight. Complicated, haunted, and always trying to do better than his past.

13. Ami Mizuno

Anime: Sailor Moon

Sailor Mercury was rocking blue hair before half this list existed. Ami is the brains of the Sailor Guardians, a shy honor student who fights with water and ice and out-thinks every enemy she meets. Kind, studious, and quietly one of the most dependable characters in the entire series.

14. Nefertari Vivi

Anime: One Piece

Vivi is the princess who sailed with the Straw Hats and earned every bit of their loyalty. Her long blue hair suits a leader willing to risk everything for her kingdom of Alabasta. Brave, selfless, and one of the most quietly heroic allies Luffy's crew ever picked up.

15. Rin Okumura

Anime: Blue Exorcist

Rin is the son of Satan who decides to become an exorcist anyway, which is about as complicated as a heritage gets. His dark blue hair and blue flames mark him as something dangerous, but he leads with a hot temper and an even bigger heart. A troublemaker you cannot help but root for.

16. Nejire Hado

Anime: My Hero Academia

Nejire is one of UA's Big Three, and her long, flowing periwinkle hair matches a mind that bounces from question to question at light speed. Endlessly curious and cheerful, she hides serious power behind all that bubbly energy. Underestimate her and you will regret it fast.

17. Himmel

Anime: Frieren: Beyond Journey's End

Himmel is the hero whose legend hangs over all of Frieren, the blue-haired leader of the party that once saved the world. Even in flashback he radiates warmth and quiet wisdom, and his kindness echoes through the whole series long after he is gone. Proof a character can define a story without much screen time.

18. Sayaka Miki

Anime: Puella Magi Madoka Magica

Sayaka is the magical girl whose story quietly breaks your heart. Bright blue hair, a hero's ideals, and a wish made for someone else set her on one of the most tragic arcs in the genre. Loyal to a fault and painfully human, she lingers with you long after the credits roll.

19. Aladdin

Anime: Magi

Aladdin is the small, cheerful magician at the center of Magi, his blue braid swinging as he stumbles into world-shaping adventures. Behind the childlike grin sits one of the most powerful and wise figures in the entire series. Warm, curious, and far deeper than he first lets on.

20. Mukuro Rokudo

Anime: Katekyo Hitman Reborn!

Mukuro is a mist-shrouded schemer with a grudge against the world and a habit of never quite dying. Calm, cryptic, and always three plans ahead, he is the kind of antagonist who slowly becomes impossible not to like. His dark blue hair suits a character built almost entirely out of mystery. Endlessly cool.

Honorable mentions

A few blue-adjacent favorites that just missed the strict cut: Inosuke Hashibira, whose black hair only turns blue at the tips, and Bulma, whose shade has drifted between blue, teal, and green across the years. Tenya Iida keeps Class 1-A in line with his dark blue mane, and Konan folds paper into deadly art over in Naruto.

Blue hair, unforgettable every time

Loyal maids, feral Espadas, disaster goddesses: blue haired anime characters cover an enormous range, and that is exactly the fun of it. The color might be the reason they first caught your eye, but it is the personalities underneath, Rem's devotion, Aqua's chaos, Grimmjow's pride, that make them stick. Pick a favorite and you are really picking a character, not a shade.

If you love this kind of deep dive into the characters who make anime worth watching, come hang out with us at Kaminari, where our newsletter covers the news, reviews, and fan debates worth your time. Tell us who we missed. We always have room for one more.

FAQs

Who are the most famous blue hair anime characters?

Rem from Re:Zero is probably the single most famous, right up there with Rei Ayanami and Rimuru Tempest. Hinata Hyuga and Grimmjow round out the names most fans picture first when the topic comes up.

Who are the best female anime characters with blue hair?

Rem, Hinata Hyuga, Rei Ayanami, Esdeath, and Aqua lead the pack, covering everything from loyal maids to terrifying generals to chaotic goddesses. There is a lot more range here than the color alone suggests.

Who are the best blue-haired anime guys?

For the guys, Grimmjow, Jellal, Rin Okumura, and Franky stand out, ranging from feral villains to loyal shipwrights. Kuroko and Nagisa are the top male light blue haired anime characters, both landing on the quieter, calmer side.

Which characters with light blue hair stand out?

Aqua, Kuroko, Nagisa Shiota, and Rimuru Tempest are the go-to characters with light blue hair, mostly sitting on the calmer or more cheerful end of the personality scale.

Who has short or long blue hair in anime?

Among anime characters with short blue hair, Rem and Kuroko lead the way. For long blue hair characters, Nejire Hado and Nefertari Vivi are the standouts, both wearing it well past the shoulders.

Title: 20 INFP Anime Characters You Need To Know if You're a Mediator
Summary: Round up 20 INFP anime characters, the gentle Mediators of anime, with Alphonse Elric and Mob up top. 🕊️
Meta Title: INFP Anime Characters: 20 Gentle Mediators
Meta Description: Meet the INFP anime characters who prove quiet idealists steal the show, gentle dreamers with steel cores. Join Kaminari for more anime lists.
Author: devin-morris
Content:
INFPs, the Mediators of the MBTI world, are the quiet idealists: introverted, imaginative, and guided by a private set of values they will not compromise on. Anime is full of them, because the gentle dreamer with a steel core underneath makes for exactly the kind of character you fall for. We gathered twenty of the most INFP anime characters and, just as importantly, the reason each one fits.

The type runs on Introverted Feeling, which is a quiet inner compass that measures everything against personal values rather than outside rules. Add a vivid imagination and a deep well of empathy, and you get characters who feel things intensely, dream big, and refuse to betray who they are even when it would be so much easier to.

You will find gentle healers, tortured artists, and soft-spoken idealists here, spanning long-running shonen and Ghibli classics alike. We stuck to characters the community broadly agrees are Mediators, and parked the hotly debated ones in the honorable mentions where they belong. Let's get into it.

The 20 most INFP anime characters

Each pick below comes with the trait that seals it, whether that is a stubborn moral core, a runaway imagination, or a heart worn permanently on the sleeve. These are the anime characters who are INFP through and through.

1. Alphonse Elric

Anime: Fullmetal Alchemist

Al is the Mediator heart of Fullmetal Alchemist. Trapped in a suit of armor, he never loses his gentleness, his empathy, or his unshakable belief that people are worth saving. His whole journey runs on a private moral code he will not bend, even when the world hands him every reason to. Pure Introverted Feeling.

2. Shigeo “Mob” Kageyama

Anime: Mob Psycho 100

Mob is what an INFP looks like with god-tier powers and zero ego about it. He keeps his enormous feelings locked inside until they overflow, values kindness over winning, and just wants to be a good person on his own quiet terms. The most gentle overpowered protagonist in anime, and it is not close.

3. Legoshi

Anime: Beastars

Legoshi is a textbook Mediator in the body of a large, frightening wolf. He is soft-spoken, endlessly conflicted about his own instincts, and forever weighing what is right against what is easy. His entire story is an INFP wrestling with identity and morality. Beastars practically runs on his inner monologue.

4. Shizuku Tsukishima

Anime: Whisper of the Heart

Shizuku is the INFP artist in her purest form. A bookish daydreamer who lives inside her stories, she sets out to write a whole novel simply because she has to know whether she can. Her arc is about chasing a private creative dream and measuring herself against her own ideals rather than anyone else's expectations. Textbook Mediator.

5. Orihime Inoue

Anime: Bleach

Orihime feels everything at full volume and tucks most of it behind a bright smile. Imaginative to the point of daydreaming mid-conversation, fiercely loyal, and motivated purely by protecting the people she loves, she is one of anime's warmest INFPs. Her strength was always emotional first.

6. Atsushi Nakajima

Anime: Bungo Stray Dogs

Atsushi is an INFP still learning to like himself. Gentle, self-doubting, and haunted by his past, he keeps choosing compassion anyway, extending kindness to people who have not earned it because his values quietly demand it. Watching him slowly find his own worth is the emotional spine of the show.

7. Natsume Takashi

Anime: Natsume's Book of Friends

Natsume is a Mediator to his core, a gentle boy who keeps choosing kindness even after a lonely childhood spent being feared for the spirits only he could see. Rather than wield the book of yokai names he inherits, he spends the series quietly giving each one back, guided entirely by his own soft sense of what is right. Sensitive, introspective, and slow to trust, he reaches for connection anyway, one careful bond at a time. His whole story is empathy quietly outlasting old wounds.

8. Muichiro Tokito

Anime: Demon Slayer

Muichiro drifts through half his scenes lost in his own head, which is about the most INFP thing a character can do. Behind the daydreaming is a gentle soul who reconnects with his buried feelings and fights for the people he quietly loves. Dreamy on the surface, deeply devoted underneath.

9. Crona

Anime: Soul Eater

Crona is anxiety, sensitivity, and a desperate need for genuine connection wrapped into one fragile character. Timid and easily overwhelmed, they still hold onto a tender inner world that the story slowly coaxes into the light. An INFP shaped by pain, but an INFP right to the core.

10. Tamaki Amajiki

Anime: My Hero Academia

Tamaki would rather melt into a wall than talk to anyone, and every INFP knows the feeling. Wildly anxious in public, he is also a loyal, big-hearted hero who believes in his friends far more than he believes in himself. The gap between his crippling nerves and his real strength is peak Mediator.

11. Izumi Miyamura

Anime: Horimiya

Miyamura hides a soft, artistic soul under a shy, closed-off exterior, which is a very INFP way to survive high school. Once he lets people in, he turns out to be gentle, thoughtful, and quietly devoted. His entire arc is about a rich inner world finally being seen and accepted.

12. Yuri Katsuki

Anime: Yuri on Ice

Yuri feels his sport with an intensity that borders on painful. Anxious, self-critical, and driven by love for the craft rather than trophies, he skates from a place of pure personal meaning. That values-first passion, wrapped in a bundle of nerves, is textbook Mediator energy.

13. Rikka Takanashi

Anime: Love, Chunibyo & Other Delusions

Rikka lives half inside a fantasy world of her own making, which is the INFP imagination taken to its most literal extreme. Her delusions turn out to be a shield for real grief, and underneath the theatrics is a sensitive kid processing loss the only way she knows how. Dreamer and mourner in one.

14. Yamaguchi Tadashi

Anime: Haikyuu!!

Yamaguchi spends most of Haikyuu quietly doubting himself in Tsukishima's shadow, which any INFP will recognize instantly. Sensitive, loyal, and desperate to contribute without making a fuss, he finds his courage through sheer personal conviction rather than swagger. His trembling, hard-won growth is some of the most relatable material in the show.

15. Meiko “Menma” Honma

Anime: Anohana

Menma is gentleness distilled. Even lingering as a wistful presence, she is defined by pure, uncomplicated love for her friends and a quiet wish to see them happy. Her whole arc runs on emotional idealism, the belief that the people she loves deserve peace. Heartbreak in Mediator form.

16. Nunnally vi Britannia

Anime: Code Geass

Surrounded by a family of schemers and warlords, Nunnally stays impossibly soft. She dreams of a gentle world and holds onto kindness as an actual political ideal, which in Code Geass makes her practically a unicorn. Her sweetness is not naivety, it is a value she chooses on purpose. Deeply INFP.

17. Chihiro Ogino

Anime: Spirited Away

Chihiro starts as a scared, sulky kid and grows into someone brave through pure heart. She wins over an entire spirit world not with power but with kindness, sincerity, and stubborn loyalty to the people she cares about. Her quiet moral compass carries the whole film. A young INFP finding her strength.

18. Rakka

Anime: Haibane Renmei

Rakka is a gentle, searching soul trying to make sense of her own existence, which is about as INFP as a premise gets. Deeply empathetic and quietly troubled, she keeps reaching out to others while wrestling with her own need for meaning. Haibane Renmei is essentially a meditation on a Mediator finding peace.

19. Chiyuki

Anime: Death Parade

Chiyuki carries an enormous amount of buried feeling behind a composed surface. Introspective and emotionally raw once her walls finally come down, she pushes the whole show to reckon with empathy and the weight of a single human life. Her quiet, values-driven arc is Mediator storytelling at its most affecting.

20. Toboe

Anime: Wolf's Rain

Toboe is the softest heart in a harsh, wandering world. The youngest of the pack, he leads with affection and loyalty, forming bonds the others are too guarded to risk. Gentle to a fault and guided almost entirely by feeling, he is an INFP trying to hold onto tenderness in a story that keeps testing it.

Honorable mentions

A few characters who turn up on plenty of INFP lists, but whose typing the community genuinely argues over: Shinji Ikari and Gaara (both pulled toward ISFP by some), Kaneki Ken (a very popular INFJ pick), and Nausicaä (frequently typed ENFJ for how decisively she leads). All Mediator-adjacent, all worth the debate.

Why we love a good Mediator

For all their shyness, INFP anime characters tend to be the ones who stay with you longest, because their strength is the kind you have to look closely to notice. Al's compassion, Mob's restraint, Legoshi's quiet conscience, it all comes from the same place: a heart that simply refuses to compromise. That quiet integrity is exactly why the Mediators so often end up being everyone's favorite.

If typing your favorite characters is your idea of a good time, you will fit right in at Kaminari, where our newsletter digs into the anime, characters, and debates worth caring about. Come tell us which INFP we got wrong. We know you have opinions.

FAQs

What is an INFP personality type?

INFP stands for Introverted, Intuitive, Feeling, and Prospecting, nicknamed the Mediator. These are quiet idealists who lead with a strong inner set of values, a rich imagination, and deep empathy, caring more about authenticity and meaning than rules or status. Plenty of INFP personality type anime characters put that on full display.

What anime characters are INFP?

Some of the clearest, least-debated examples are Alphonse Elric, Mob from Mob Psycho 100, Legoshi, Atsushi Nakajima, and Shizuku Tsukishima. Each one leads with empathy, imagination, and a personal moral code, which are the core traits of the Mediator type.

Who is the most INFP anime character?

Alphonse Elric and Mob are the two most cited, and it is easy to see why. Both are gentle, deeply principled, and quietly powerful, choosing kindness at every turn even when it costs them. Either one lands as a near-perfect Mediator.

Are there famous female INFP anime characters?

Absolutely. Orihime Inoue, Mitsuri Kanroji, Shizuku Tsukishima, Nunnally, and Rikka Takanashi are all strong female INFPs, each guided by empathy and a private set of ideals rather than outside expectations.

How can you tell if a character is INFP?

Look for a dominant sense of personal values, an idealistic streak, a vivid imagination, and a tendency to feel deeply but privately. The anime characters who are INFP usually hate conflict, dream big, and stay loyal to what they believe no matter the pressure.

Title: 20 Iconic Blonde Anime Characters Every Fan Needs To Know
Summary: Rank 20 blonde anime characters, male and female, with Naruto and Lucy leading heroes, icons, and villains. ✨
Meta Title: Blonde Anime Characters: 20 Heroes and Villains
Meta Description: See the blonde anime characters who define their whole series, loud heroes and terrifying villains alike. Come hang out with Kaminari for more.
Author: devin-morris
Content:
Blonde is one of anime's most common hair colors, and also one of its most iconic. It lands on loud shonen heroes, elegant knights, chaotic goddesses, and terrifying villains alike. We rounded up twenty of the best blonde anime characters, male and female, and ranked them on the personalities that made them matter, not just the golden hair.

Anime blonde hair shows up in every genre and shade. You will spot bright yellow haired anime characters like Zenitsu, golden-braided icons like Edward Elric, and popular blonde anime characters who basically defined their whole series. Roughly half this list is female, which fits, since some of the most beloved blondes in anime are women.

Long-running shonen legends, modern scene-stealers, and a villain or two round out the roster, every pick earning its place on charisma and character. Let's get into it.

The 20 best blonde anime characters

Gathered from every corner of anime and ranked loosely by how unforgettable they are, not by shade. Heroes, icons, and a couple of villains, all sharing one very golden trait.

1. Naruto Uzumaki

Anime: Naruto

Naruto's spiky blonde hair is the face of shonen itself. The loudmouth orphan who dreamed of being Hokage turned relentless optimism into an actual superpower, dragging an entire world toward peace through sheer refusal to give up on anyone. Few characters have inspired more fans to keep going.

2. Lucy Heartfilia

Anime: Fairy Tail

Lucy is the heart the whole Fairy Tail crew orbits. A celestial mage who fights alongside her summoned spirits like family, she is kind, determined, and braver than she gives herself credit for. Her warmth and loyalty are a big part of why the guild feels like home.

3. Edward Elric

Anime: Fullmetal Alchemist

Ed is a genius, a hothead, and a kid carrying the weight of one terrible mistake. His golden braid and short temper are iconic, but it is his fierce devotion to his brother and his refusal to sacrifice a single life that make him unforgettable. One of anime's best-written protagonists, blonde or otherwise.

4. Usagi Tsukino

Anime: Sailor Moon

Usagi is the blueprint nearly every blonde heroine after her borrowed from. A crybaby who would rather nap than fight, she still carries the whole world on her shoulders and protects her friends with a heart of pure gold. Sailor Moon proved a gentle, silly girl could be the strongest one in the room.

5. Sanji

Anime: One Piece

Sanji is all sharp suits, sharper kicks, and a soft spot a mile wide. The Straw Hats' cook fights with his legs to keep his hands safe for cooking, never raises them against a woman, and would starve before letting a crewmate go hungry. Chivalry and firepower in one blonde package.

6. Saber

Anime: Fate/stay night

Saber carries herself like the king she once was. Noble, disciplined, and bound by an unbending code of honor, she commands every scene she is in without ever raising her voice. Behind the regal calm is a leader haunted by the weight of her choices. Pure presence.

7. Winry Rockbell

Anime: Fullmetal Alchemist

Winry is the mechanic who keeps Ed standing, literally. Brilliant with automail and fierce about the people she loves, she anchors Fullmetal Alchemist with warmth and a wrench that doubles as a weapon. Her strength is the quiet, steady kind that holds everyone else together.

8. Zenitsu Agatsuma

Anime: Demon Slayer

Zenitsu spends most of Demon Slayer screaming, crying, or both, which makes it all the sweeter when his bright yellow hair flashes and he cuts down a demon in his sleep. Under the cowardice is a loyal, big-hearted kid who fights hardest for the people he loves. Yellow-haired chaos with a spine of steel.

9. Marin Kitagawa

Anime: My Dress-Up Darling

Marin is sunshine given a personality. An outgoing cosplayer who wears her passions with zero shame, she coaxes the withdrawn Gojo out of his shell through pure enthusiasm and genuine kindness. Her confidence and warmth made her an instant modern favorite.

10. Kurapika

Anime: Hunter x Hunter

Kurapika is calm on the surface and a storm underneath. The last of his clan, he channels his grief into an ice-cold quest for justice that costs him more and more of himself along the way. His blonde hair and gentle manner hide one of anime's most driven, tragic hearts.

11. Historia Reiss

Anime: Attack on Titan

Historia spends half of Attack on Titan pretending to be someone else, and the other half becoming who she really is. Underneath the fake smile is a girl with a spine of iron who decides to define herself on her own terms. Her quiet transformation into a real leader is one of the show's best.

12. Misa Amane

Anime: Death Note

Misa is often the first blonde many fans picture, and for good reason. Devoted to the point of danger and driven entirely by love, she throws herself into Light's scheme with a reckless loyalty that reshapes the whole story. Chaotic, tragic, and impossible to ignore.

13. Loid Forger

Anime: Spy x Family

Loid is the master spy pretending to be a normal dad, and slowly, hilariously, becoming one for real. Cool, competent, and quietly overwhelmed by the fake family he grows to actually love, he anchors Spy x Family with equal parts action and heart. The blonde super-dad we all want.

14. Meliodas

Anime: The Seven Deadly Sins

Meliodas looks like a harmless blonde kid and is anything but. The Dragon Sin of Wrath hides centuries of power and pain behind a lazy grin, fiercely protective of the people he loves and terrifying when they are threatened. Deceptively soft on the surface, ancient underneath.

15. Kento Nanami

Anime: Jujutsu Kaisen

Nanami brought exhausted-office-worker energy to Jujutsu Kaisen and fans adored him for it. His dirty blonde hair and no-nonsense professionalism hide a deeply principled man who treats being a decent adult as its own kind of heroism. The mentor everyone quietly wishes they had.

16. Darkness

Anime: KonoSuba

Darkness is a noble crusader who is also a complete disaster, which is exactly the KonoSuba way. Genuinely brave and devoted to her ideals, she throws herself into danger with a conviction the rest of the party can only envy. Chaotic, loyal, and far more capable than she ever lets on.

17. Tsunade

Anime: Naruto

Tsunade is the legendary Sannin who became Hokage, and one of the strongest women in anime. Beneath the gambling habit and the temper is a healer carrying enormous grief who still chooses to protect her village with everything she has. Power and heartbreak in equal measure.

18. Katsuki Bakugo

Anime: My Hero Academia

Bakugo starts as pure explosive rage and slowly, grudgingly, grows into a real hero. His ash-blonde spikes match a personality that runs permanently hot, but underneath the fury is a fierce competitor who genuinely wants to be the best for the right reasons. One of anime's best-earned redemptions.

19. Violet Evergarden

Anime: Violet Evergarden

Violet begins as a soldier who barely understands her own feelings and grows into someone who helps others put theirs into words. Her golden hair frames a quiet, careful soul learning what love actually means, one letter at a time. One of anime's most quietly devastating arcs.

20. Tanya von Degurechaff

Anime: The Saga of Tanya the Evil

Tanya is what happens when a ruthless salaryman gets reincarnated as a small blonde girl and handed command of a nation's military. Cold, calculating, and gleefully willing to do terrible things in the name of efficiency, she is one of anime's most memorable blonde villains. Terrifying in the most entertaining way possible.

Honorable mentions

A few more blondes worth a shout: Riza Hawkeye keeping Mustang alive in Fullmetal Alchemist, Armin outthinking everyone in Attack on Titan, Dio Brando chewing scenery as JoJo's most iconic villain, and Tamaki Suou charming all of Ouran High School Host Club. Any one of them could headline a list of their own.

The gold standard

Naruto's spiky yellow, Saber's regal gold, Tanya's villainous platinum: blonde anime characters have given us some of the medium's most iconic heroes, sweethearts, and villains. The color might catch your eye first, but it is the personalities, Lucy's warmth, Ed's fire, Tanya's menace, that keep these characters at the top of every list. Pick a favorite and you are really picking a whole story.

If you love breaking down the characters who make anime worth watching, come hang out with us at Kaminari, where our newsletter rounds up the news, reviews, and debates worth your time. Tell us which blonde we snubbed. We can take it.

FAQs

Who are the best female blonde anime characters?

Some of the most beloved female blondes in anime are Lucy Heartfilia, Sailor Moon, Saber, Winry Rockbell, and Tsunade. They range from gentle sweethearts to legendary warriors, proving the color fits every kind of heroine.

Who are the most popular blonde anime characters?

Naruto Uzumaki and Edward Elric usually top the list of popular blondes, with Sanji, Kurapika, and Lucy close behind. These are the blondes most fans picture the moment the topic comes up.

What shades of blonde appear in anime?

Anime blonde hair covers a huge range. You get golden tones on characters like Edward Elric, dirty blonde anime characters like Kento Nanami, platinum blonde and ash shades on the cooler types, and the occasional strawberry blonde or bleached look. If it lands anywhere near gold, anime has drawn it.

Which anime characters have short or long blonde hair?

For anime characters with short blonde hair, Naruto, Bakugo, and Nanami lead the way. For anime characters with long blonde hair, Lucy Heartfilia, Saber, and Tsunade stand out, wearing it long and unmistakable.

Are there blonde anime villains?

Plenty. Tanya von Degurechaff is a standout among blonde anime villains, ruthless and unforgettable, and Dio Brando from JoJo might be the most iconic blonde villain of all. Blonde hair suits a menacing smile as well as a heroic one.

Title: Top 20 Pink-Haired Anime Characters You Can’t Help but Love
Summary: Line up 20 pink haired anime characters, male and female, Sakura and Anya beside anime's scariest yanderes. 🌸
Meta Title: Pink Haired Anime Characters: 20 Bold Picks
Meta Description: Browse the pink haired anime characters who own every scene, cheerful sweethearts and chilling yanderes alike. Check out Kaminari for more.
Author: devin-morris
Content:
Pink hair might be rare in real life, but in anime it is practically a personality type. It lands on cheerful sweethearts, terrifying yanderes, hot-blooded fighters, and deadpan geniuses alike. We rounded up twenty of the best pink haired anime characters, male and female, and ranked them on the personalities that make the color memorable.

Pink tends to signal something specific: softness that hides an edge, or an energy too big to blend in. Some of these characters weaponize the sweetness, some subvert it completely, and a few just own it louder than everyone around them. Roughly half the list is female and half is not, because pink hair belongs to everyone.

You will find shonen legends, magical girls, chaos gremlins, and at least one full-on psychopath here. Every pick earns its place on character, not just the color. Let's get into it.

The 20 best pink haired anime characters

Gathered from every corner of anime and ranked loosely by how unforgettable they are. Heroes, villains, and a whole spectrum of pink in between.

1. Sakura Haruno

Anime: Naruto

Sakura is the pink-haired face of an entire generation of anime fans. She starts out insecure and overshadowed, then claws her way into becoming one of the strongest medical ninja alive, punching craters into the battlefield. Her growth from bystander to powerhouse is one of Naruto's quiet triumphs, and the pink hair grew right along with her.

2. Zero Two

Anime: Darling in the Franxx

Zero Two is equal parts charm and danger, and she knows it. Wild, unpredictable, and fiercely lonely underneath, she upends the whole series the moment she arrives. Her devotion to finding her “darling” drives the story, and her pink hair, horns included, became an instant fandom icon. Impossible to forget, for better or worse.

3. Anya Forger

Anime: Spy x Family

Anya is pure chaotic serotonin. The telepathic little schemer holds a fake family together while reading everyone's minds and reacting with the most meme-able faces in modern anime. Her pink hair and enormous heart made her a phenomenon almost overnight. Nobody roots harder for peace than a kid just trying to keep her weird family together.

4. Yuno Gasai

Anime: Future Diary

Yuno is the yandere the trope practically named itself after. Sweet and doting one moment, coldly lethal the next, she will protect the boy she loves at absolutely any cost, body count included. Her soft pink hair is the perfect bait-and-switch for one of anime's most genuinely frightening characters. Devotion turned into a weapon.

5. Madoka Kaname

Anime: Puella Magi Madoka Magica

Madoka looks like a standard magical-girl lead and is anything but. Gentle, selfless, and quietly brave, she spends her story resisting a system built to break girls like her, then makes a choice that reshapes reality out of pure compassion. Her pink twin-tails hide one of anime's most quietly powerful heroines.

6. Chika Fujiwara

Anime: Kaguya-sama: Love Is War

Chika is the engine of chaos that makes Kaguya-sama sing. Bubbly, unpredictable, and gloriously bad at the mind games everyone else is playing, she derails every scheme with pure whimsy. Her pink hair matches an energy that cannot be contained, and her infamous dance broke the internet for good reason.

7. Lucy

Anime: Elfen Lied

Lucy is innocence and horror in the same character. Behind the long pink hair and childlike alter ego is a Diclonius capable of unimaginable violence, shaped by a lifetime of cruelty. Her tragic split between gentleness and rage makes her one of anime's most haunting figures. Not for the faint of heart.

8. Mine

Anime: Akame ga Kill

Mine is a sniper with a sharp tongue and a soft center she would rather die than admit to. Proud, prickly, and devastatingly accurate, she fights for a better world from a distance while slowly letting people in. Her pink hair suits a personality that refuses to be ignored. All attitude, real heart.

9. Perona

Anime: One Piece

Perona went from ghostly villain to one of the stranger allies orbiting the Straw Hats, pink hair following her every step. Obsessed with all things cute and quick to send her negative-energy ghosts at anyone who annoys her, she is equal parts menacing and ridiculous. Chaos with a bow in its hair.

10. Mina Ashido

Anime: My Hero Academia

Mina, better known as Pinky, radiates pure joy across every scene she is in. Bubbly, social, and quick to bring her classmates together, she is the glue of Class 1-A even if her acid Quirk gets more attention. The pink hair and pink skin make her unmissable, and the warmth makes her unforgettable.

11. Nonon Jakuzure

Anime: Kill la Kill

Nonon is loyalty wrapped in attitude and a conductor's uniform. Sharp-tongued and endlessly devoted to Satsuki, she leads with a confidence that borders on menace and a bond that never once wavers. Her pink hair fits a character who is all bark, plenty of bite, and secretly a big softie for the people she trusts.

12. Hitori “Bocchi” Gotoh

Anime: Bocchi the Rock!

Bocchi is social anxiety given a guitar and a mop of pink hair. Painfully shy and prone to spiraling into elaborate fantasies, she also happens to be a musical genius the second nobody is watching. She turned relatable awkwardness into one of the most beloved recent characters in anime. A genuine introvert icon.

13. Yuji Itadori

Anime: Jujutsu Kaisen

Yuji is the beating heart of Jujutsu Kaisen, pink spikes over a black undercut and all. Freakishly strong, endlessly kind, and determined to make sure people can die with dignity, he carries an impossible burden with a smile. His refusal to abandon anyone is the moral center the whole series leans on.

14. Natsu Dragneel

Anime: Fairy Tail

Natsu will tell you his hair is salmon, not pink, and then set something on fire to change the subject. The Dragon Slayer runs on loyalty, appetite, and a bottomless will to protect his guild. Hot-blooded and reckless in the best way, he is one of shonen's most beloved pink-haired (sorry, salmon-haired) heroes.

15. Kusuo Saiki

Anime: The Disastrous Life of Saiki K.

Saiki is a godlike psychic who wants absolutely nothing to do with being special. Deadpan, exhausted, and permanently trying to live a normal life his powers will not allow, he narrates his own chaos with world-class sarcasm. His pink hair and glowing antennae are honestly the least strange thing about him.

16. Gowther

Anime: The Seven Deadly Sins

Gowther is the stoic one, the Sin who spent most of his existence not understanding emotions at all. A doll built long ago by a demon, he processes feelings like puzzles and slowly learns to be human, which makes his rare moments of warmth land hard. His soft pink hair belies a genuinely unsettling, fascinating character.

17. Cherry Blossom

Anime: SK8 the Infinity

Cherry Blossom, also known as Kaoru, skates with the elegance of a poet and the pettiness of a lifelong rival. Calm and refined on the surface, he loses his composure spectacularly the second his best-friend-slash-nemesis shows up. His long pink hair suits a character who takes both his art and his grudges very seriously.

18. Kisumi Shigino

Anime: Free!

Kisumi is the friendly, easygoing charmer who somehow knows everyone. Warm and social where the Free! main cast tends toward brooding, he brings an effortless lightness to every scene he wanders into. His pink hair matches a personality built almost entirely out of good vibes. Sometimes a character just needs to be nice, and Kisumi nails it.

19. Szayelaporro Granz

Anime: Bleach

Szayelaporro is a mad scientist Espada who treats every battle like a lab experiment. Vain, brilliant, and thoroughly unhinged, he is the kind of villain who monologues about his own perfection right up until it backfires spectacularly. His pink hair fits a character who is equal parts genius and theatrical disaster.

20. Koby

Anime: One Piece

Koby starts as a timid errand boy and grows into one of the Marines' most promising young officers, all without losing his fundamental decency. His pink hair marks a character whose quiet determination and moral backbone make him one of One Piece's best underdog stories. Proof that soft-spoken and strong are not opposites.

Honorable mentions

A few more pink-haired favorites, including a couple whose color is not strictly pink: Mitsuri Kanroji, whose hair famously fades from pink into green, and Sukuna, whose pink is streaked through with black. Add Yachiru Kusajishi causing havoc in Bleach and Crona bringing the anxiety in Soul Eater, and you have a whole second list.

Why pink always steals the scene

Hero, villain, sweetheart, or psychopath, pink haired anime characters have a way of grabbing your attention and refusing to let go. The color reads as soft, which is exactly why so many writers use it to hide an edge, whether that is Yuno's menace, Sakura's raw strength, or Saiki's bottomless sarcasm. Pick a favorite and you are really picking one of anime's boldest quiet design choices.

If you love pulling apart the characters who make anime worth watching, come hang out with us at Kaminari, where our newsletter rounds up the news, reviews, and debates worth your time. Tell us which pink-haired legend we left out. We will hear you out.

FAQs

Who is the most popular pink haired anime character?

Yuji Itadori, Natsu Dragneel, Anya Forger, and Sakura Haruno consistently top fan votes for pink haired anime characters. Each one is a household name in their series, which is why they lead nearly every ranking built around the color.

Are there male pink haired anime characters?

Plenty. Yuji Itadori, Natsu Dragneel, Kusuo Saiki, and Gowther are some of the most popular, proving pink hair is far from a female-only trait. The medium is full of hot-blooded, deadpan, and stoic pink-haired guys.

Who is the most iconic female pink haired character?

Sakura Haruno is probably the most iconic, having represented pink hair for an entire generation of Naruto fans. Zero Two, Yuno Gasai, and Anya Forger are right behind her, each unforgettable for very different reasons.

Why do so many anime characters have pink hair?

Pink is visual shorthand. It signals softness, playfulness, or innocence at a glance, which writers love to either lean into or completely subvert. A pink-haired character stands out instantly, and the contrast between a gentle color and a fierce personality makes for memorable designs.

Are pink haired characters usually heroes or villains?

Both, and that is the fun of it. For every cheerful hero like Anya or Mina, there is a terrifying pink haired anime character like Yuno or Lucy waiting to flip the script. The color works just as well for a sweetheart as it does for a menace.

Title: Top 20 White-Haired Anime Characters Who Completely Stole the Show
Summary: Gather 20 white haired anime characters, powerhouses, mentors, and changed heroes, with Gojo and Kaneki up top. ❄️
Meta Title: White Haired Anime Characters: 20 Powerhouses
Meta Description: Discover the white haired anime characters anime saves for its strongest, oldest, and most changed. Head to Kaminari for more anime lists.
Author: devin-morris
Content:
White hair is anime shorthand for pay attention. It lands on the strongest, the oldest, the most otherworldly, and the most changed, which is why a white-haired character almost always carries a certain weight. We rounded up twenty of the best white haired anime characters, male and female, and ranked them on the personalities that earn all that presence.
