It is a lean, underrated war story.

The build match is the grounded historical war saga: a real invasion, a brutal defensive fight, and warriors reckoning with survival and loss, all without a shred of fantasy. Like Vinland Saga, it dramatizes an actual historical conflict and finds its drama in the human cost of battle. The build link is the grounded, fantasy-free story of a young man shaped by violence and loss, fighting through a brutal world while a quiet relationship offers a glimpse of something better. Ash's arc, forged by abuse and vengeance yet reaching for peace, rhymes with Thorfinn's, and the series shares Vinland Saga's unflinching maturity. Author: devin-morris
Content:
Still chasing that Plus Ultra feeling after Deku's rise from quirkless kid to the next Symbol of Peace? Plenty of anime like My Hero Academia deliver the same mix: an underdog who trains at an institution for young heroes, a diverse power system, a fierce rival, a found-family class, and the heroes-versus-villains stakes that make every fight matter. No show replaces it, but the closest ones carry that same hopeful, heroic spirit.

The timing makes a watchlist worth it, too. My Hero Academia is bowing out: the manga wrapped in 2024, and the anime's Final Season arrived in 2025 to bring Deku's journey to a close. If you are still catching up before the end, our My Hero Academia filler list points you to the parts that matter.

We ranked these from closest match to loosest, judged on one thing: how much each shares My Hero Academia's actual build, a superhero shonen where an underdog trains within a hero institution, with a diverse power system, a rival, a found-family class, and a hopeful, spectacle-driven coming-of-age. There is a quick table up top, plus honest notes at the end.

11 shows like My Hero Academia at a glance

If you just want the fast read, here is the whole roster. The Similarity column is our call on how close each one gets to My Hero Academia itself, not how good the show is on its own.

The anime most like My Hero Academia, ranked

Here are the anime like My Hero Academia that genuinely share its build, ranked from the closest match to the loosest. The Similarity Rating is our read on how near each one gets to My Hero Academia specifically, not how good the show is overall, and we kept the stars to whole numbers. The build we are measuring against is simple: a superhero shonen where an underdog trains at a hero institution, with a diverse power system, a rival, a found-family class, and a hopeful, spectacle-driven coming-of-age.

1. Black Clover

Similarity Rating: 5/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: Asta is born with zero magic in a world where magic defines social standing, so he grinds his body into a weapon and fights his way up the Magic Knight ranks on sheer stubbornness. He receives a rare, ostracized anti-magic grimoire, competes against his elite foster brother Yuno, and takes a competitive squad entrance exam. Both chase the highest public rank: the Wizard King. Along the way he joins the rowdy, misfit Black Bulls squad.

Black Clover is the fantasy mirror to Deku's journey. Asta is born completely without magic in a society where magic defines social standing, which is Deku being Quirkless almost exactly, and through pure physical grit and relentless training he receives a rare, ostracized power, takes a competitive squad entrance exam, and aims for the highest public rank: the Wizard King, the setting's Symbol of Peace. The powerless-outcast origin, the training grind, and the climb toward the top title are MHA's structure in a fantasy coat. Our Black Clover filler list helps you skip the slow patches.

2. Kaiju No. 8

Similarity Rating: 5/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: Kafka Hibino cleans up kaiju corpses for a living, having repeatedly failed the Defense Force entrance exams, until a freak incident turns him into a kaiju himself. A washed-up man suddenly handed power he never expected, he finally breaks into the elite force that fights giant monsters, where he must master a dangerous, monstrous power while keeping it hidden. The monster-of-the-week structure plays like a modernized hero association. The animation is a genuine spectacle.

Kaiju No. 8 is the closest match to MHA's modern institutional hero-defense work. Kafka is an older underdog who repeatedly failed the official entrance exams, finally breaking into a defense force where he has to master a dangerous, monstrous power while keeping it hidden, which mirrors MHA's tactical military rescue raids, specialized gear, and public-safety operations alongside younger prodigies. The professional-hero institution, the underdog's late shot, and the hide-your-power pressure all land exactly like MHA.

3. World Trigger

Similarity Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: When gates to another world open and monsters called Neighbors pour through, a defense organization named Border holds the line using special weapons called Triggers. Osamu Mikumo is a low-ranked agent with weak stats who makes up for it with grit and strategy, fighting to climb an explicit ranking system alongside his team. The series runs on tactical team battles rather than raw power. It rewards patience with some of the sharpest fights in the genre.

World Trigger is the definitive peer for MHA's tactical battle drills, Class 1-A exams, and squad-based strategy. Osamu is weak and stays tactically dependent on his team, winning through positioning, utility triggers, and synergy rather than raw power, and the B-Rank Wars capture the exact feel of an extended, high-strategy U.A. Sports Festival. The ranked ladder and the team missions mirror MHA's class and hero rankings closely. It is calmer and more tactical, but on the squad-strategy front it is one of the closest here.

4. Blue Exorcist

Synopsis: Rin Okumura learns he is the son of Satan, born with blue flames sealed in a blade, a heritage that makes him feared and hated. He enrolls at True Cross Academy to become an Exorcist and forge his own identity, taking classes, completing license exams, and training in specialized combat roles. He must also learn to control an overwhelming, volatile power that could destroy his body and reputation if he loses his grip. He fights beside classmates who become his found family.

Blue Exorcist is a direct hero-academy structure. Set inside True Cross Academy, students take classes, complete license exams, and train in specialized combat roles, Knight, Dragoon, and Doctor, exactly the shape of U.A.'s hero course. Rin also has to control an overwhelming, volatile power that threatens to destroy his body and his reputation if he loses control, which is Deku's early struggle with One For All in a different coat. The academy structure and the volatile-power burden make it a close fit.

Anime Overall Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Shinra, a boy with flame-powered feet and a nervous grin, joins Company 8 to lay the Infernals to rest and uncover the truth behind the phenomenon. The squad becomes a tight-knit family, and the mythology runs deeper than it first appears. The action is flashy and stylish.

Fire Force matches MHA's civic-superhero framework. The Special Fire Soldiers are licensed civil servants responding to citywide emergencies and monstrous threats in a modern metropolis, complete with public-image concerns, rival-brigade politics, and rookie tournament games, all of which could have been lifted from U.A. and the Hero Association. Shinra even dreams of becoming a hero who saves people with a smile, which is Deku's exact ambition. The licensed-hero institution and the modern-city stakes make it a strong match.

Synopsis: Naruto Uzumaki is the dead-last of his ninja class, mocked by a village that fears the beast sealed inside him, and he decides he will become its leader anyway. He trains at the ninja academy, climbs the ranks, and chases the dream of becoming Hokage. His rivalry with the prodigy Sasuke defines him, while his squad becomes the family he never had. It is one of the foundational shonen epics.

Naruto is the primary direct inspiration for My Hero Academia. Kohei Horikoshi drew heavily from its DNA: an outcast protagonist carrying immense destructive power, an academy training arc, high-stakes testing, with the Chunin Exams directly influencing the Sports Festival, and a volatile, complex childhood rivalry, with Deku and Bakugo mirroring Naruto and Sasuke. The underdog origin, the training institution, and the rival who defines the hero are the roots MHA grew from. Our Naruto filler list points you to the parts that matter.

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: At a school for weapon-wielding meisters and the human weapons they partner with, teams of students hunt evil souls to turn their blades into legendary death-scythes. Maka and her scythe partner Soul, along with a cast of oddballs, face witches, madness, and monsters. The series pairs stylish, gothic-cartoon visuals with fast, funny action. It is weird, bold, and endlessly energetic.

Soul Eater shares MHA's specialized academy setup for gifted youths. At the Death Weapon Meister Academy, students balance classes, homework, and field assignments to collect souls and protect civic peace, the same school-trains-young-protectors shape as U.A. It even shares MHA's animation studio in BONES and the classroom dynamic, though its style is much more gothic, eccentric, and irreverent. The academy-and-missions build lands for MHA fans, even with the weirder tone.

8. Jujutsu Kaisen

Similarity Rating: 3/5 ⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 5/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: Yuji Itadori swallows a cursed object to protect his friends and is pulled into a hidden war between sorcerers and curses, the monsters born from human fear. He enrolls at a secret school for sorcerers and trains alongside a ranked organization of specialists. The threats escalate fast and the cost is brutal. The animation delivers some of the most explosive fights around.

Jujutsu Kaisen shares MHA's modern training-school setting in Jujutsu High, its student squads, and an outcast protagonist hosting an unwieldy power. It sits in the lower half here because it drops the public hero licensing, the large classroom ensemble, and the optimism, trading them for a much darker, lethal world of sorcery with minimal actual classroom time. The school-and-squads bones are there, but the hopeful, hero-course heart that defines MHA is not. Our Jujutsu Kaisen filler list marks what matters.

9. Blue Lock

Synopsis: After Japan's World Cup humiliation, a ruthless program locks three hundred of the country's best teenage strikers into a facility designed to forge one supreme egotist, pitting them against each other in brutal elimination games. Isagi is an unremarkable striker who discovers a hidden instinct as the pressure mounts. The series is a high-stakes psychological sports thriller. It is as intense as any battle shonen.

Blue Lock is a sports wildcard, but mechanically it is nearly identical to an intense U.A. training camp. Hundreds of teenagers are isolated in a high-pressure training facility, forced to analyze their distinct individual weapons, their version of Quirks, and put through brutal elimination rounds and tactical team scenarios. The institution, the diverse abilities, and the relentless ranking echo MHA's structure closely. It is soccer rather than superheroes, which keeps it lower, but the training-facility build is a surprising match.

10. One Punch Man

Similarity Rating: 3/5 ⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 5/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: Saitama has trained so hard that he can defeat any opponent with a single punch, which has left him bored out of his mind. He registers with the Hero Association, a ranked bureaucracy of professional heroes, and goes largely unrecognized despite being the strongest of them all. The series skewers superhero tropes while delivering spectacular fights. It is as funny as it is gorgeous.

One Punch Man shares MHA's exact civic setting: a modern metropolis governed by a bureaucratic Hero Association with ranked C-Class to S-Class heroes. The pro-hero bureaucracy and the rankings come from the same world-structure. It ranks low here because it is a satirical deconstruction, with Saitama beginning at peak power and zero room to grow, inverting Deku's struggle and removing the school-and-training progression entirely. The superhero setting lines up, but the underdog growth that powers MHA is gone.

11. Hunter x Hunter

Similarity Rating: 3/5 ⭐⭐⭐

Synopsis: Gon sets out to become a Hunter and find the father who left him, starting with a punishing exam that weeds out the weak. The journey opens into one of the most carefully built power systems in anime, alongside a crew of friends who grow into something like family. It gets darker and more complex than its bright start suggests. Many fans call it the best shonen ever made.

Hunter x Hunter features brilliant tactical combat and an iconic, high-stakes license exam arc, but it lacks the core MHA framework. There is no regular school environment, no civic superhero system, and no central class ensemble; it is an unpredictable, globe-trotting adventure that progressively turns into a dark psychological study. Keep the heroics going as the Symbol of Peace era ends

Still feeling that will of fire after Naruto's long run from village outcast to Hokage? Plenty of anime like Naruto deliver the same mix: an underdog who dreams of the top, a fierce rival who pushes him there, a found family worth fighting for, a power system to master, and the training, tournaments, and tragic backstories that make every victory land. No show replaces it, but the closest ones carry that same spirit.

Naruto itself is a finished, foundational classic, with the original run and Shippuden long complete, and while a 20th-anniversary remake has been teased for years, it keeps getting delayed, so there is no new main series on the way. If you are still working through the saga, our Naruto filler list points you to the parts that matter.

We ranked these from closest match to loosest, judged on one thing: how much each shares Naruto's actual build, a long-running shonen battle epic with an underdog who dreams of the top, a fierce rival, a power system, found-family bonds, and real emotional backstory. There is a quick table up top, plus honest notes at the end.

The anime most like Naruto, ranked

Here are the anime like Naruto that genuinely share its build, ranked from the closest match to the loosest. The Similarity Rating is our read on how near each one gets to Naruto specifically, not how good the show is overall, and we kept the stars to whole numbers. The build we are measuring against is simple: a long-running shonen battle epic with an underdog who dreams of the top, a fierce rival, a power system, found-family bonds, and real emotional backstory.

1. Black Clover

Similarity Rating: 5/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: Asta is an orphan born with zero magic in a world where magic is status, so he grinds his body into a weapon and fights his way up the Magic Knight ranks on sheer stubbornness. He also houses a sealed, forbidden anti-magic demon, and competes fiercely against his elite foster brother Yuno, a prodigy raised alongside him. Both chase the same dream: to become the Wizard King, the nation's military leader. Along the way he joins the rowdy, misfit Black Bulls squad.

Black Clover is the closest modern equivalent to Naruto. An orphaned, loud underdog born without the power everyone values, a sealed forbidden force inside him, a fierce rivalry with his elite foster brother, a misfit squad, and a fight to become the nation's leader are all lifted straight from the Naruto playbook. “Become the Wizard King” is “become Hokage,” and the Asta-and-Yuno dynamic is Naruto and Sasuke in all but name. For the most direct match to Naruto's spirit, this is it.

2. Jujutsu Kaisen

Similarity Rating: 5/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 5/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: Yuji Itadori swallows a cursed object to protect his friends and is pulled into a hidden war between sorcerers and curses, the monsters born from human fear. He enrolls at a secret school for sorcerers and trains alongside a ranked organization of specialists. The threats escalate fast and the cost is brutal. The animation delivers some of the most explosive fights around.

Jujutsu Kaisen is the clearest match for Naruto's core squad and power dynamics, borrowing the Team 7 layout almost directly. Yuji is the headstrong physical vessel housing a destructive ancient demon in Sukuna, Megumi is the stoic, black-haired summoner who fills the rival-ally slot, Nobara is the headstrong female teammate, and Gojo is the overpowered, white-haired sensei with his eyes covered, the same four-piece shape as Naruto, Sasuke, Sakura, and Kakashi. The fights even lean on hand-to-hand martial arts layered with tactical energy management, just like chakra control. Our Jujutsu Kaisen filler list marks what matters.

3. My Hero Academia

Similarity Rating: 5/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: Izuku Midoriya is born without a superpower in a world where almost everyone has one, mocked and counted out, until the greatest hero alive sees his heart and passes him a legacy. He enrolls at an elite hero academy, trains relentlessly, and sets his sights on becoming the number one hero. His explosive rival Bakugo pushes him at every turn, and his class becomes a found family. It is bright, earnest, and emotionally charged.

My Hero Academia is the modern spiritual successor to Naruto's growth philosophy. Deku starts as a powerless outcast who inherits a legendary power from his mentor, learns to manage the self-destructive toll that power takes on his body, and climbs through high-stakes tournament and exam arcs, all while wrestling with a volatile childhood rivalry in Bakugo. The inherited-power burden, the training-and-tournament structure, and the rival who mirrors the hero are Naruto's DNA almost beat for beat. Our My Hero Academia filler list keeps your watch clean.

4. Blue Exorcist

Similarity Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: Rin Okumura learns he is the son of Satan, born with blue demonic flames sealed away in a blade, a heritage that makes him feared and hated. Rather than embrace it, he enrolls at an academy to become an Exorcist and forge his own identity, training to hunt demons and one day take down his own father. He fights beside classmates who become his found family. The tone balances real darkness with warmth and humor.

Blue Exorcist shares Naruto's exact demon-sealed-inside-an-outcast trope. Rin carries blue flames sealed in a blade, enrolls in an academy to become an Exorcist, and works through squad exercises, license exams, and friction with his prodigy brother Yukio. The hated-for-what-he-is origin, the sealed power, the training school, and the prodigy-sibling tension rhyme closely with Naruto carrying the Nine-Tails. It is smaller in scope and scale, which keeps it mid-list, but the sealed-outcast-plus-academy build is a solid fit.

5. Hunter x Hunter

Similarity Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 5/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: Gon sets out to become a Hunter and find the father who left him, starting with a punishing exam that weeds out the weak. The journey opens into one of the most carefully built power systems in anime, alongside a crew of friends who grow into something like family. It gets darker and more complex than its bright start suggests. Many fans call it the best shonen ever made.

Hunter x Hunter is the primary structural blueprint for Naruto's most iconic early arcs. The Hunter Exam was the direct template for the Chunin Exams, and its Nen system laid the groundwork for how chakra affinities and conditions work, so the mechanics feel like an ancestor. If you loved the high-IQ, tactical puzzle-solving combat of the Forest of Death, this is its closest peer. It is deeper and more cerebral than Naruto, but the exam-and-power-system build runs straight through both.

6. Demon Slayer

Similarity Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 5/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: After his family is slaughtered by a demon and his sister is turned into one, Tanjiro joins the Demon Slayer Corps to avenge them and find a cure. Training in a sword-breathing technique, he climbs the Corps' ranks toward the elite Hashira while hunting the demons that prey on humanity. The series pairs breathtaking animation with real emotional stakes. It is one of the most beloved anime of its era.

Demon Slayer matches Naruto's emotional tone and its discipline ladder. Tanjiro leads an earnest journey alongside a quirky squad, using elemental combat styles in the Breathing Forms that function much like elemental jutsu, and he climbs a strict military hierarchy, the Demon Slayer Corps ranks that top out at the Hashira. Most of all, it humanizes its tragic villains right at the moment of their defeat, which is Naruto's cycle-of-hatred theme almost exactly. There is no central rival or top-title dream, which keeps it a touch lower, but the tone and the structure are a genuine fit.

7. Yu Yu Hakusho

Similarity Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 5/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: Delinquent teenager Yusuke Urameshi dies saving a child, then gets a second chance at life as a Spirit Detective, tasked with policing threats from the demon world. He gathers a crew of rivals-turned-allies and fights his way through tournaments and demon invasions. The series blends action, comedy, and real heart. It is a foundational classic from Hunter x Hunter's creator.

Yu Yu Hakusho is the classic ancestor that helped define the squad-shonen format Naruto runs on. It brings together a four-person unit of contrasting personalities, each with specialized spirit abilities, who work dark spirit investigations and the kind of tournament arcs that shaped 2000s battle anime. Yusuke's brash growth, the found-family crew, and those tournament staples all carry a clear Naruto flavor. It is older and shorter, but the squad-and-tournament build is a genuine fit.

8. World Trigger

Similarity Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: When gates to another world open and monsters called Neighbors pour through, a defense organization named Border holds the line using special weapons called Triggers. Osamu Mikumo is a low-ranked agent with weak stats who makes up for it with grit and strategy, fighting to climb an explicit ranking system alongside his team. The series runs on tactical team battles rather than raw power. It rewards patience with some of the sharpest fights in the genre.

World Trigger is the closest match for the team-based, tactical chess matches of the Chunin Exams. The protagonist is physically weak and stays that way, so fights are won through squad coordination, positioning, trigger utility, and reading an opponent's habits rather than sudden power-ups, which is the Naruto exam at its most strategic. The ranked ladder and the team missions mirror the Hidden Leaf's structure closely. It is calmer and more tactical than Naruto overall, but on the strategic-team-battle front it is a strong fit.

9. Mashle: Magic and Muscles

Similarity Rating: 3/5 ⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 3/5 ⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: Mash Burnedead is born with no magic in a society where magic is everything, so he bluffs his way into an elite magic academy, aiming to earn the title of Divine Visionary and secure his family's safety by solving every obstacle with absurd physical strength. His rivals are prodigies who were handed everything. The tone is deadpan and frequently hilarious. It plays like a magic-school shonen crossed with a bodybuilding gag.

Mashle is a direct play on the Rock Lee core theme of hard work over natural talent. Mash is born completely without magic in an elitist magical society, relying on extreme physical training, body conditioning, and blunt-force solutions to counter complex spells and high-ranking academy elites, which is Rock Lee's whole ethos stretched into a lead role. The underdog-outworks-the-prodigies spirit and the magic-academy ranks are a clear Naruto echo. It is lighter and more of a gag comedy, so it sits lower, but the hard-work-beats-talent build is a clear match.

10. Bleach

Similarity Rating: 3/5 ⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll, Hulu

Synopsis: Ichigo Kurosaki gains the powers of a Soul Reaper and is thrust into a hidden war, guarding the living from corrupted spirits and battling his way through the ranks of the afterlife. As the threats escalate, so does his power, across sprawling arcs full of memorable fighters. The final saga has been brought to life with stunning modern animation. It is a cornerstone of the shonen battle genre.

Bleach is a direct contemporary from the Big Three era, with top-tier hype and sword combat to match. Ichigo is a reactive protector with no grand political ambitions, so there is no Hokage-style dream driving him, which is why it sits lower here than its fame might suggest. But it shares the escalating, tier-based power systems, the fierce rivalries, and the major military factions of the Soul Society, all of which Naruto fans will recognize. Our Bleach filler list sorts out where to start.

11. Soul Eater

Similarity Rating: 3/5 ⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: At a school for weapon-wielding meisters and the human weapons they partner with, teams of students hunt evil souls to turn their blades into legendary death-scythes. Maka and her scythe partner Soul, along with a cast of oddballs, face witches, madness, and monsters. The series pairs stylish, gothic-cartoon visuals with fast, funny action. It is weird, bold, and endlessly energetic.

Soul Eater shares the academy setting and the student-trio squad structure under a specialized organization in the DWMA, which echoes the Hidden Leaf's academy and its three-person teams. The power system and the found-family dynamics land for Naruto fans. It ranks lowest here because its tone is much more eccentric, comedic, and gothic-urban-fantasy than Naruto's grounded, earnest ninja journey, but the academy-and-squad build is a genuine fit.

A few anime similar to Naruto that watch differently

Search around for anime related to Naruto and two names come up a lot that do not quite fit the hopeful, underdog-shonen build. They are worth your time. We just want the match to feel honest.

Boruto is the direct sequel, set in the same village with the next generation and the exact same ninja system, so it is less a show like Naruto and more literally more Naruto, best watched as a continuation once you are caught up. Attack on Titan gets recommended for its epic scope and its themes of hatred and war, but it is a grim, tragic deconstruction rather than a hopeful coming-of-age, so it trades Naruto's heart for despair. Both are worth watching. Just know that one is the continuation and the other is a very different beast.

Carry the will of fire to your next watch

Naruto is a finished, foundational classic, and while a 20th-anniversary remake has been teased and delayed for years, there is no new main series on the way, which leaves a real hole for fans to fill. The good news is that plenty of shows carry a piece of what made it special. Start at the top with Black Clover and Jujutsu Kaisen for the closest squad-and-rivalry matches, carry the growth philosophy with My Hero Academia, or play the tactical chess of World Trigger. The whole point of a good list of anime like Naruto is to keep that mix of heart, rivalry, and relentless growth going long after the credits roll on Shippuden.

While you line it all up, come hang out with us at Kaminari, where our weekly newsletter rounds up the shows worth your time, the news that actually matters, and takes written for people who love this stuff as much as you do. We will keep flagging the best shonen epics as they land, so you never miss the next one.

FAQs

Is there an anime exactly like Naruto?

Not a perfect twin, but two come very close. Black Clover is the closest modern equivalent, with an orphan underdog, a sealed forbidden power, a foster-brother rival, and a fight to become the nation's leader, while Jujutsu Kaisen borrows the Team 7 squad layout almost directly. Each nails the core of what makes Naruto tick.

What is the best anime like Naruto?

For the closest structure, Black Clover and Jujutsu Kaisen lead the pack with their underdog-and-squad builds. If you want the epic scale and depth instead, Hunter x Hunter and Bleach are the best anime like Naruto for a saga you can sink hundreds of hours into.

What anime is like Naruto Shippuden?

For the darker, higher-stakes feeling of Shippuden specifically, the long battle epics fit best: Bleach, Jujutsu Kaisen, and Hunter x Hunter all deliver the sprawling arcs, the escalating stakes, and the matured characters that made Shippuden hit harder than the original run.

Is there a new Naruto anime or remake?

A 20th-anniversary project of four new animated episodes was announced in 2023, but it was pulled before release and has been delayed ever since, with no confirmed date. In the meantime, the sequel series Boruto continues the story in the same world with the next generation.

Where can you watch anime like Naruto?

Most of these stream on Crunchyroll, including Naruto itself, with Bleach also available on Hulu. Streaming rights shift by region and over time, so double-check what is available where you are before you settle in.

Content:
Still haunted by that blue butterfly after Satoru's desperate race to save Kayo and catch a hidden killer? Plenty of anime like Erased deliver the same mix: a grounded thriller where an ordinary person gets the power to reach into the past, a frantic race to prevent a death, a mystery to unravel, and a bittersweet, protective heart underneath the suspense. No show replaces it, but the closest ones grip you the same way.

Erased itself is a finished, self-contained classic, a tight twelve-episode thriller from 2016 with no anime sequel on the way, so once that gut-punch ending lands, there is nowhere to go but outward. The good news is that the time-travel-thriller space it helped define is full of hidden gems.

We ranked these from closest match to loosest, judged on one thing: how much each shares Erased's actual build, a grounded psychological thriller driven by a time-travel or do-over mechanic, where the hero races to prevent a death and unmask a hidden threat, with high suspense and a bittersweet, protect-the-vulnerable heart. The anime most like Erased, ranked

Here are the anime like Erased that genuinely share its build, ranked from the closest match to the loosest. The Similarity Rating is our read on how near each one gets to Erased specifically, not how good the show is overall, and we kept the stars to whole numbers. The build we are measuring against is simple: a grounded psychological thriller driven by a time-travel or do-over mechanic, where the hero races to prevent a death and unmask a hidden threat, with high suspense and a bittersweet, protective heart.

1. Summer Time Rendering

Similarity Rating: 5/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 5/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Disney+, Hulu

Synopsis: Shinpei returns to his small island hometown for the funeral of his childhood friend, who drowned saving a girl, only to learn her death may not have been an accident. As a deadly mystery unfolds, he gains the ability to loop back in time whenever he dies, using it to protect the people he loves. The island setting is cozy and sinister at once. It is a tense, twist-filled thriller that rarely lets up.

Summer Time Rendering is the undisputed closest match to Erased. It is a murder mystery set in an isolated seaside town, where the protagonist's time resets let him gather forensic clues one loop at a time, all while he races against an encroaching threat that keeps targeting the people he loves. The reset-to-investigate-and-save structure, the small-community setting, and the constant ticking-clock dread are Erased's exact shape. The threat is supernatural rather than a lone human killer, which is the one real difference, but nothing else lines up this precisely.

2. Higurashi: When They Cry

Similarity Rating: 5/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: A boy moves to a sleepy rural village and settles into easy days with new friends, until a cycle of paranoia, murder, and madness reveals itself beneath the calm. The story loops through variations of the same cursed summer, each one peeling back more of the mystery. The sweetness curdles into horror without warning. It is a cult classic of the mystery-horror genre.

Higurashi matches Erased on the setting, the tight group of elementary and middle-school peers, and the dark psychological terror of slowly realizing a killer is operating among ordinary townspeople. The friends relive the same cursed stretch of time, using the resets to work out what they have to change to break the tragedy and save everyone, which is Satoru's investigation turned into a puzzle box. It is bloodier and more openly horror than Erased, which is the main difference in tone, but the rural-town dread and the loop-to-solve-and-save build are a remarkably close fit.

3. Tokyo Revengers

Similarity Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: Takemichi, a down-on-his-luck adult, learns that his middle-school girlfriend has been killed by a violent gang, then discovers he can leap twelve years into the past. He throws himself into changing the events that led to her death, infiltrating the gang as a kid to rewrite a brutal future. Each trip back raises the stakes. It blends delinquent drama with real time-travel tension.

Tokyo Revengers is the closest mechanical twin to Erased's time-leap. An adult failure leaps a decade back into his younger, school-age self to undo a tragic death, then jumps between past actions and the present to watch the timeline ripple, which is Satoru's Revival scaled up to years instead of minutes. Like Erased, it is an ordinary person throwing himself into his own past to save people he could not protect. The setting is gang violence rather than a child-killer mystery, but the time-leap-to-prevent-a-death mechanic and the bittersweet stakes line up closely.

4. Steins;Gate

Similarity Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 5/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: A self-styled mad scientist named Okabe discovers that his makeshift microwave can send text messages into the past, and his tinkering spirals into something far bigger than he bargained for. When a close friend's death becomes the price of his meddling, he is forced to leap through time again and again to undo it. The first half is a slow burn, the second is relentless. It is widely considered one of the greatest anime ever made.

Steins;Gate matches Erased's sheer psychological agony and its desperate, repeated timeline alterations to prevent a loved one's murder. Okabe, like Satoru, is forced to reach into the past again and again, each attempt costing him more, in a race to reach the one outcome where the person he loves survives. It trades the snowy rural school for an urban tech-thriller lab, so the texture is different, but the grounded time-travel and the frantic save-them-this-time core are pure Erased.

5. Orange

Similarity Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: Naho receives a letter from her twenty-six-year-old self, begging her to change the past and save a new transfer student, Kakeru, from a future tragedy. As she pieces together what is coming, she and her friends try to reach a boy quietly drowning in grief. The story is gentle, aching, and deeply kind. It is a quiet gut-punch about regret and the people we wish we had saved.

Orange captures the quiet, melancholic emotional core of Erased. Using foreknowledge of the future, Naho reaches out to save a socially isolated peer from trauma and a looming death, and the whole story runs on the same ache of hindsight and the desperate wish to protect someone vulnerable before it is too late. It is a grounded drama rather than a thriller, so the suspense is gentler, but the reach-back-to-save-a-lonely-kid build is a direct match for Erased's heart.

6. The Promised Neverland

Similarity Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll, Hulu

Synopsis: Three gifted children at a seemingly idyllic orphanage discover the horrifying truth about their home and the caretaker they trusted, and begin a tense game of wits to escape before they are next. Every plan is a gamble, every glance from the adults a threat. The first season is a masterclass in suspense. It is a nerve-shredding thriller about children outwitting a predator.

The Promised Neverland puts children in a psychological chess match, trying to outwit an adult predator who holds all the institutional power and authority over them, which is the beating heart of Erased's main arc. Like Satoru shielding Kayo and his classmates from a trusted adult, the kids here have to read, plan, and outmaneuver a smiling threat to survive, with vulnerable young lives on the line and a clock running down. Its first season is the match, and there is no time-travel, which keeps it off the top, but the protect-the-children-from-a-predator thriller build is a strong fit.

7. Re:Zero

Similarity Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 5/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: Subaru is yanked into a fantasy world and quickly discovers his one power: when he dies, he returns to an earlier checkpoint, keeping his memories. He uses it, at enormous psychological cost, to claw his way toward outcomes where the people he loves survive. The deaths are brutal and the trauma is real. It is a punishing, gripping deconstruction of the wish-fulfillment isekai.

Re:Zero shares Erased's checkpoint-rewind mechanic and the psychological trauma of repeatedly failing to stop impending murders. Subaru's Return by Death drops him to an earlier save point every time he dies, forcing him to relive horror until he finds the path where the people he loves survive, which is Satoru's Revival turned merciless. It is set in high fantasy rather than a grounded town, which keeps it a notch lower, but the rewind-to-prevent-deaths engine and the toll it takes are a close match.

8. Monster

Similarity Rating: 3/5 ⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 5/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Prime Video

Synopsis: A brilliant surgeon saves the life of a young boy, only to watch that boy grow into a charming, remorseless killer, and spends years hunting him across Europe to undo the evil he allowed to live. It is a slow, sprawling, deeply human thriller with one of anime's great villains. Every character feels real. It is a towering achievement in suspense.

Monster is the closest match if you strip the sci-fi away entirely: a dark, realistic, grounded detective chase hunting down a terrifying human killer across bleak European environments. Like Satoru, Dr. Tenma is an ordinary man consumed by the need to stop a murderer and protect the vulnerable, trading spectacle for dread, character, and suspense. There is no time-travel or do-over here, which is why it sits lower on an Erased list specifically, but for the realistic-thriller-and-hidden-killer half of the show, nothing does it better.

9. ID:Invaded

Similarity Rating: 3/5 ⭐⭐⭐

Anime Overall Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Watch on: Crunchyroll

Synopsis: A disgraced detective dives into the shattered minds of serial killers, reconstructed as surreal dreamscapes, to piece together clues and catch them in the real world. Each case is a puzzle built from a murderer's psyche. The structure is inventive and the mysteries are tightly plotted. It is a cerebral sci-fi detective thriller.

ID:Invaded is a high-concept mystery thriller focused on entering the psychological minds of active serial killers to stop their murders before time runs out, which lines up with Erased's investigative, catch-the-killer side. The pressure of getting inside a criminal's logic to prevent the next death echoes Satoru's attempts to outthink the man hurting his classmates. There is no time-travel and the vibe is colder and more procedural, which keeps it lower, but the race-to-stop-a-murderer build is a solid fit.

10. Another

Similarity Rating: 3/5 ⭐⭐⭐

Of everything here, this is the undisputed closest match, because Yoshihiro Togashi created it himself, and it reads as the rough prototype for Hunter x Hunter. The core four-man team of Yusuke, Kuwabara, Kurama, and Hiei is the direct precursor to Gon, Leorio, Kurapika, and Killua, and it runs on the same escalating tournament arcs, dark spirit-world rules, and tactical mind games. Naruto is the most direct structural heir to Hunter x Hunter. Masashi Kishimoto drew heavily from Togashi: the Hunter Exam directly inspired the Chunin Exams, Nen's conditions and types shaped chakra nature manipulation, and Kurapika's tragic pursuit of the Phantom Troupe was the template for Sasuke and the Uchiha clan massacre. Jujutsu Kaisen is heavily influenced by Togashi's battle logic. Bleach is Jujutsu Kaisen's foundational inspiration, and the connection is personal: Gege Akutami has cited Tite Kubo as the reason he became a mangaka. The build shows it everywhere. That is Okabe's problem in a different coat: use what you learned last time, change one variable, and run it again. The dread, the twist-heavy plotting, and the cost of every reset line up exactly. FAQs

Is there an anime exactly like Code Geass?

Not a perfect twin, but two come very close. Death Note is the mastermind match, a brilliant, morally-grey genius who gains a supernatural power and creates a masked alter ego to remake the world, while Guilty Crown is the direct spiritual sibling, written by a Code Geass co-creator and built on the same occupied-Japan, soul-power, resistance template. Each captures the core of what makes Code Geass tick.

What is the best anime like Code Geass?

For the closest overall match, Death Note and Guilty Crown lead the pack, one for the scheming anti-hero, the other for the shared blueprint. If you want the mecha-and-military-war side specifically, Mobile Suit Gundam 00 and 86 are the best anime like Code Geass to jump into next, both pairing tactical mecha combat with real political weight.

Why are anime like Code Geass and Death Note always paired together?

Because Lelouch and Light are the two icons of the same archetype: the brilliant, charismatic anti-hero who gains a supernatural power, builds a masked revolutionary identity, and wages a secret, morally-grey war to remake a broken world through a battle of wits. If you searched for anime like Code Geass and Death Note, you are chasing that exact genius-anti-hero thrill, and each is the first show fans point to for the other.

Is there a new Code Geass anime?

Yes. Beyond the original two seasons, the franchise released the Lelouch of the Re;surrection film in 2019 and the all-new series Code Geass: Rozé of the Recapture in 2024, which follows a fresh cast years later. More projects have been announced, so the saga is actively expanding.

Where can you watch anime like Code Geass?

Most of these stream on Crunchyroll, including the original Code Geass, with Legend of the Galactic Heroes also on Prime Video. Streaming rights shift by region and over time, so double-check what is available where you are before you settle in.
